title: The Story of Nur al-Din Ali ibn-Bakkar and the Slave-Girl Shams al-Nahar

paragraphs.en: I heard, O happy King, that Abu al-Hasan ibn-Tahir, a wealthy druggist in Baghdad, was well-respected for his honesty and kindness. His shop was frequented by many, including Nur al-Din Ali ibn-Bakkar, a Persian prince's descendant known for his virtues and beauty.
paragraphs.zh: 我听说，幸福的国王啊，阿布·阿斯兰·本泰赫是一位在巴格达声名卓著的药剂师，以诚实和仁慈著称。他的店铺常有顾客光顾，其中包括努尔丁·阿里·本巴卡儿，他是波斯王子的后裔，以其美德和美貌闻名。

paragraphs.en: One day, ten virgins entered the shop, followed by Shams al-Nahar on a gray mule adorned with red silk and gems. Her beauty was unmatched; even the full moon seemed pale in comparison. Abu al-Hasan rose to greet her, seating her on a luxurious cushion while he stood respectfully.
paragraphs.zh: 一天，十名处女走进店铺，随后是骑着一匹披着红丝和宝石装饰的灰色骟马的沙姆斯·纳哈尔。她的美貌无与伦比，就连满月也显得黯然失色。阿布·阿赫桑站起身迎接她，让她坐在一张豪华的坐垫上，自己则恭敬地站立在一旁。

paragraphs.en: Nur al-Din Ali ibn-Bakkar saw Shams al-Nahar and was overwhelmed. His face flushed and paled as he tried to approach her but almost fainted out of respect. She looked at him with playful eyes and smiled sweetly, saying, "My lord, I come to you, yet you flee from me."
paragraphs.zh: 努尔丁·阿里·本巴卡尔见到沙姆斯·纳哈尔时不禁为之倾倒。他的脸色忽红忽白，试图靠近她却几乎因敬畏而晕厥。她用戏谑的眼神看着他，甜甜地笑道：“我的主人，我来找你，你却躲避我。”

paragraphs.en: He kissed the ground and replied, "When I saw you, I lost my senses; for she is the sun that in heaven dwells."
paragraphs.zh: 他吻了地面，回答道：“一见到你，我就神魂颠倒；她犹如天上的太阳。”

paragraphs.en: Shams al-Nahar summoned Abu al-Hasan and Nur al-Din Ali. She asked where they had found the young man named Ali ibn-Bakkar, who was a descendant of kings. When she learned he was Persian, she instructed them to bring him to her quarters so she could entertain them in Baghdad.
paragraphs.zh: 沙姆斯·纳哈尔召见了阿布·阿萨兰和努尔丁·阿里。她问他们是在哪里找到那位名叫阿里·本巴卡儿的年轻人的，他是一位国王的后裔。得知他是波斯人后，她吩咐他们将他带到自己的住处，在 Baghdad 为他们准备一番娱乐。

paragraphs.en: Fearing her displeasure, Abu al-Hasan agreed.
paragraphs.zh: 怕她不高兴，阿布·哈桑只好答应了。

paragraphs.en: The next day, Shams al-Nahar's maid arrived and invited the men to visit her mistress. Disguised, they followed the girl into the caliph’s palace. They were led to a room that resembled Paradise, filled with luxurious couches and cushions.
paragraphs.zh: 第二天，奴斯海勒的女仆前来邀请男人们去见她的主人。他们乔装改扮后，跟着女孩进入了哈里发的宫殿。他们被带到了一个宛如天堂般的地方，到处都是豪华的卧榻和软垫。

paragraphs.en: After settling in, the black maid served them a feast of suckling lambs, fatted chickens, birds like grouse and quail, pickles, and candies.
paragraphs.zh: 安顿下来后，那个黑奴女仆为他们准备了一桌丰盛的佳肴，有乳猪、肥鸡、野兔和鹌鹑等肉类美食，还有腌制食品和糖果。

paragraphs.en: Abu al-Hasan then recounted their visit to Shams al-Nahar, describing the opulent setting and the sumptuous meal they enjoyed.
paragraphs.zh: 阿布·哈桑随后讲述了他们拜访沙姆斯·纳哈尔的情景，描述了那里的豪华布置以及他们享用的丰盛宴席。

paragraphs.en: After our meal, two golden basins were brought for us to wash our hands. Incense was then offered, and we perfumed ourselves. Rosewater scented with musk in crystal bowls adorned with carved camphor and ambergris was used to scent ourselves before returning to our couches.
paragraphs.zh: 用餐之后，我们面前摆上了两个金盆，用来洗手。随后焚香，我们又以香水沐浴了一番。晶莹剔透的碗中盛着掺有麝香和龙涎香的玫瑰水，香气四溢，我们在返回卧榻之前便以此来增添几分雅致。

paragraphs.en: The maid led us into another chamber where a silk carpet covered the floor under a domed ceiling supported by hundred pillars, each topped with a golden bird or beast. We admired the carpet's gold ground and white and red roses, which mirrored the colors of the dome. Crystal and gold trays filled with jewels were placed on tables in the room.
paragraphs.zh: 女仆领我们走进另一个房间，那里铺设着丝绒地毯，下方是拱顶天花板，由上百根柱子支撑，每根柱子顶端都雕饰着金鸟或金兽。我们赞叹那块金色底地上绣着白玫瑰和红玫瑰的地毯，其色彩与穹顶相映生辉。房间里桌上摆满了晶莹剔透、镶嵌珠宝的银托盘。

paragraphs.en: At the far end, numerous colorful couches stood before arched windows opening onto a garden that seemed to have the same carpet pattern on its floor. Water flowed from a large pond to a smaller one surrounded by sweet basil, lilies, and narcissus in gold-inlaid pots. Branches intertwined thickly, heavy with ripe fruits, which dropped into the water as birds swooped down, their wings clapping and songs filling the air.
paragraphs.zh: 在远处，各式色彩斑斓的长沙发排列在拱形窗户前，窗外是一片花园，地面上仿佛铺着与室内相同的地毯图案。水从一个大池塘流入周围种有香蜂草、百合和金边球根花的小池塘中。枝条交织繁茂，果实累累，鸟儿飞掠而过，翅膀拍打声和悦耳的歌声在空气中回荡，水面上不时落下几颗成熟的果子。

paragraphs.en: On either side of the pond stood sandalwood couches covered in silver, each occupied by a damsel more radiant than the sun, dressed gorgeously and holding lutes or other musical instruments. Their music blended with the cooing of birds, while the wind wafted through, lifting roses and dropping fruits into the water.
paragraphs.zh: 池塘两侧各摆放着几座银饰覆盖的檀香木榻，每张榻上坐着一位比太阳还要耀眼的少女，她们身着华服，手中或弹拨着琵琶，或持着其他乐器。鸟鸣与乐声交织在一起，微风轻拂，吹落了玫瑰花瓣和果实，飘入水中。

paragraphs.en: Dazzled by such splendor, we marveled at the beauty and grandeur of the scene, reflecting on the abundance of means and blessings displayed before us.
paragraphs.zh: 被如此华美的景象所震撼，我们不禁赞叹眼前美景与宏大气派，感慨面前展现的种种财富与恩赐之丰盛。

paragraphs.en: Nur al-Din Ali ibn-Bakkar turned to Abu al-Hasan and said, "A man of reason and wisdom would surely appreciate this scene. If I were in your position, I would feel the same way." He continued, "Beauty brought me here, and fate visited me with this affliction.
paragraphs.zh: 努尔丁·阿里·本巴卡转向阿布·哈桑说道：“一个理性而明智的人肯定会欣赏这一幕。如果我处在你的位置，也会有同样的感受。”他继续说，“美丽引我至此，命运让我承受了这场灾难。”

paragraphs.en: Since nothing prevents me from speaking, I want to know the commissioner's intention and who dares speak so openly."
paragraphs.zh: 既然我没有什么可顾虑的，我想了解一下这位委托人的意图，以及是谁如此坦率地开口说话。

paragraphs.en: Morning interrupted Shahrazad, but Dinarzad said, "Sister, what a fascinating story!" Shahrazad replied, "Wait until tomorrow! The tale will be even more amazing."
paragraphs.zh: 晨光打断了沙赫拉兹的讲述，但迪纳兹说：“姐姐，这个故事真精彩！”沙赫拉兹回答道：“等明天吧！ 故事会更加令人惊叹。”

paragraphs.en: The next night, Shahrazad recounted:
paragraphs.zh: 第二天晚上，舍赫拉查德说道：

paragraphs.en: When Nur al-Din Ali spoke, his companion Abu al-Hasan responded, "I know nothing of her intentions. But we are close to the truth; you'll soon find out. So far, everything has been wonderful and delightful."
paragraphs.zh: 当努尔·丁·阿里开口说话时，同伴阿布·哈桑回答道：“我对她的意图一无所知。但我们离真相已经很近了；你很快就会知道的。迄今为止，一切都很美妙。”

paragraphs.en: Abu al-Hasan then narrated: As they conversed, a black girl approached and ordered the damsels to sing. One tuned her lute and sang:
paragraphs.zh: 阿布·哈桑接着叙述道：正当他们交谈时，一个黑皮肤的女孩走了过来，命令女仆们唱歌。其中一个调好了琴弦，开始吟唱：

paragraphs.en: Smitten with love and ignorant of it, My heart burned with desire. No sin did I commit, save that my tears Revealed my secret fire.
paragraphs.zh: 钟情于爱却又浑然不知，我的心因渴望而燃烧。我没有犯下任何罪过，只是我的泪水泄露了我内心的火焰。

paragraphs.en: Nur al-Din Ali exclaimed, "Bravo! Wonderful!" Then she sang:
paragraphs.zh: 努尔丁·阿里脱口而出：“妙极了！太精彩了！”然后她唱了起来：

paragraphs.en: With little hope I long for thee, And what avails even the great when they desire? My sighs of passion rise to thee, As if the coldest breath is blazing fire.
paragraphs.zh: 满怀希望渺茫，我仍思念着你， 即便是权贵，在渴望时又能如何？ 我的痴情叹息飞向你， 仿佛最寒冷的呼吸也能化作熊熊烈火。

paragraphs.en: Nur al-Din Ali sighed deeply and said, "Excellent! You have sung perfectly." He then asked her to sing more, and she continued:
paragraphs.zh: 努尔丁·阿里叹了口气，说道：“太棒了！你唱得完美无瑕。”然后他让她再唱一首，她继续唱了起来。

paragraphs.en: O you whose love grows in my heart, Reign in it as you desire. A lonely heart that pines away, Where cold disdain burns like fire.
paragraphs.zh: 你在我心中越燃越烈的爱，就让它在其中自由绽放吧。一颗孤独的心啊，在这冰冷的轻蔑中煎熬如火。

paragraphs.en: Nur al-Din Ali wept, repeating a verse. Suddenly, the damsels leapt up, tuning their instruments to burst into song:
paragraphs.zh: 努尔丁·阿里流着泪，反复念诵着一句诗。突然间，女伴们一跃而起，调整好乐器，随即高歌起来：

paragraphs.en: "Glory to God who caused this moon to rise, Bringing together lover with lover."
paragraphs.zh: “赞美上帝，让他让这轮明月升起，将情人与情人相聚。”

paragraphs.en: We looked and saw Shams al-Nahar among them, moving gracefully in a gold-embroidered blue robe, her hair flowing. Ten maidservants brought a silver couch under the trees where they began to play music in unison.
paragraphs.zh: 我们仔细一看，只见沙姆斯·纳哈尔小姐正其中，身着一件绣金的蓝色长袍，长发飘逸。十名婢女抬来了一张银色的卧榻放在树下，随即她们开始齐声演奏音乐。

paragraphs.en: Then entered ten beautiful damsels, each wearing matching jewels. Among them was Shams al-Nahar. She moved with pride and coquettish grace until she sat on the couch.
paragraphs.zh: 接着，十位美貌的少女走了进来，每个人身上佩戴着相配的珠宝。其中一位便是夏姆斯·纳哈尔。她带着一种骄傲而娇媚的姿态走到沙发前坐下。

paragraphs.en: The young man watched her, biting his fingers so hard he nearly cut them.
paragraphs.zh: 年轻人盯着她看，咬得手指几乎出血。

paragraphs.en: Turning to the druggist, he said, "A man needs no explanation after seeing; nor harbors doubt after knowing." He recited:
paragraphs.zh: 转向药剂师，他说道：“亲眼所见便无需解释，亲身体验便不再怀疑。”随后他吟诵道：

paragraphs.en: "She, she alone is the source of my pain, My unrequited love and love's long moan. Since first my eyes saw her enchanting face,"
paragraphs.zh: “她，唯独她是我痛苦的根源， 未获回应的爱情和爱的漫长哀歌。 自初见她那迷人的容颜。”

paragraphs.en: Morning came, and Shahrazad fell silent. Dinarzad said, "What a strange and entertaining story!" Shahrazad replied, "Tomorrow’s tale will be stranger still."
paragraphs.zh: 晨光初现，沙赫拉兹阿德默然不语。丁尔扎德说道：“这真是个奇特而引人入胜的故事！”沙赫拉兹阿德回应道：“明天的故事将会更加离奇。”

paragraphs.en: Nur al-Din Ali ibn-Bakkar's soul was restless, seeking no peace. He wept bitterly before the druggist, who had not warned him of his situation. Abu al-Hasan consoled him, saying that Shams al-Nahar, a slave-girl from Harun al-Rashid’s palace known as the Palace of Paradise, was well-disposed toward Ali.
paragraphs.zh: 努尔丁·阿里·本巴卡的内心焦躁不安，渴望安宁却不得。他在药剂师面前痛哭流涕，而这位药剂师并未提醒他当前的困境。阿布·哈桑安慰他说，夏姆斯·纳哈尔是一位来自哈伦·拉希德宫中的女奴，被称为天堂宫殿的侍女，对阿里颇有好感。

paragraphs.en: Ali asked about her identity, and Abu al-Hasan explained she was Shams al-Nahar. He advised Ali to cherish her and be patient, for their fate lay in God's hands.
paragraphs.zh: 阿里询问她的身份，阿布·哈桑解释说她就是夏姆斯·纳哈尔。他建议阿里珍惜她，并要有耐心，因为他们的命运掌握在上帝手中。

paragraphs.en: Suddenly, from his window, Nur al-Din saw Shams al-Nahar. Their faces flushed with passion as they gazed at each other without speaking. Shams signaled the maids to bring couches near the windows.
paragraphs.zh: 突然，努尔·丁从窗口看到了沙姆斯·纳哈尔。两人面带情火，默默对视。沙姆斯示意女仆将躺椅搬到了窗边。

paragraphs.en: The girls sat down, and Shams asked one of them to sing a song about lovers yearning for each other.
paragraphs.zh: 女孩们坐了下来，沙姆斯让其中一个女孩唱一首关于恋人彼此思念的歌。

paragraphs.en: The singer tuned her lute and sang: "As lover yearned for lover, their hearts beating as one, they drank from love's sweet river, and when the two were done, on love’s shore they stood and said with bitter tears, 'Above.'"
paragraphs.zh: 歌手调好琴弦，唱道：“情人渴望着情人，心心相印，他们共饮爱河甘甜之水。情意绵绵终有时，分别之际，两人站在爱的岸边，含着苦涩的眼泪说：‘天高。’”

paragraphs.en: Shahrazad continued her story to King Shahryar. The slave-girl Shams al-Nahar sang a sweet melody that moved Nur al-Din Ali ibn-Bakkar, who asked her to sing these lines:
paragraphs.zh: 沙赫拉兹阿德继续给沙赫里亚尔王讲述故事。女奴夏姆斯·阿娜哈尔唱起一首悦耳的歌曲，触动了努尔丁·阿里·本巴卡尔的心弦。他请求她演唱这几行歌词：

paragraphs.en: "My unrequited love Has drowned my eyes with tears. O my joy, my idol, O wish of all my years, Have pity on a man Who, hopeless, mourns alone, Who keeps love in his heart And moans with love’s sad moan."
paragraphs.zh: 我的单相思 已让双眼蒙上了泪光。 哦，我心中的喜悦，我多年的渴望， 请可怜这位孤独哀悼的男子， 他满怀爱意却绝望， 与爱同声叹息。

paragraphs.en: But morning came, and Shahrazad fell silent. Dinarzad remarked, "What an intriguing tale!" Shahrazad replied, "Wait until tomorrow night if I live!"
paragraphs.zh: 但是黎明来临，沙赫拉兹默不作声。丁纳兹德说道：“这故事真是引人入胜！”沙赫拉兹达回答道：“如果我还活着，你明天晚上就能听到更多！”

paragraphs.en: The next night, Shahrazad recounted:
paragraphs.zh: 第二天晚上，舍赫拉查德说道：

paragraphs.en: Shams al-Nahar sang the verses Nur al-Din requested, then turned to another girl and said, "Sing these lines on my behalf:"
paragraphs.zh: 莎姆斯·纳哈尔唱起了努尔·丁要求的诗句，然后转向另一个女孩说道：“请替我唱这几行诗：”

paragraphs.en: "I sigh for one who, had he shared my love And felt the pain I feel, would have gone mad. I raise my voice to God, not to a man Who knows no mercy, whose hard heart is bad. If men or demons felt the love I feel, Both men and demons would such love anneal."
paragraphs.zh: 我渴望着一个倘若他也曾分享我的爱恋，感受过我所承受的痛苦，早已疯狂的人。我把声音抬向苍天，而非那无情之人的胸膛，他的心硬如铁。若人或魔能体会我所经历的爱情，无论是人或是魔都会被这份深情所熔铸。

paragraphs.en: The girl sang tenderly. Shams al-Nahar then asked another damsel to sing:
paragraphs.zh: 女孩轻声细唱。随后，沙姆斯·纳哈尔让另一位女仆也开始歌唱：

paragraphs.en: "If you remain deaf to my moans, Nor can you to me mercy show, I will not with patience endure, For how much patience to allow? My cheerless and slow-burning heart But for you would have burst aglow."
paragraphs.zh: 如果你对我哀号充耳不闻， 又怎能在我面前施以怜悯？ 我怎忍心再耐心等待， 究竟要多少耐心才能承受？ 没有你，我的心灵早已燃起希望之火。

paragraphs.en: The two lovers, flushed with passion, trembled with delight. Ali ibn-Bakkar then asked a nearby damsel to sing:
paragraphs.zh: 两位情人激情满怀，喜悦难抑。阿里·本·巴卡尔随后请 nearby 附近的一个少女唱歌：

paragraphs.en: "The time of union is too brief For such coquettish air, For you are fair and such delay Does not befit the fair."
paragraphs.zh: “相聚的时间如此短暂， 怎能容你这般娇羞？ 你如此美丽，这样的迟疑 实在有失你的风度。”

paragraphs.en: Nur al-Din Ali's tears and moans accompanied Shams al-Nahar’s song. Upon hearing his words and seeing his actions, she rose and met him at the door, where they embraced. Their love was so intense that they swooned, and the damsels carried them to a corner of the room.
paragraphs.zh: 努尔丁·阿里的眼泪和哀叹伴随着沙姆斯·纳哈尔的歌声。听到他的话，见到他的举动，她起身迎上前，在门口与他相拥。他们的爱意如此浓烈，竟双双晕了过去，侍女们将他们扶到房间的一角。

paragraphs.en: Rosewater scented with musk revived them.
paragraphs.zh: 熏着麝香的玫瑰水让他们恢复了精神。

paragraphs.en: Shams al-Nahar then asked for Abu al-Hasan, who had hidden behind a couch. The druggist emerged, greeted her, and she thanked him profusely for his kindness. She wished him well and encouraged Ali ibn-Bakkar to trust in God and persevere in his love.
paragraphs.zh: 莎姆斯·纳哈尔随后请求见阿布·阿赫桑，后者藏身于一张沙发之后。药剂师现身，向她问好，她感激不尽地感谢了他的善举。她祝他一切安好，并鼓励阿里·本巴卡信任上帝，坚持他的爱情。

paragraphs.en: Ali declared that he would never stop loving Shams until his dying day, as her love had mastered his soul. Their tears flowed like unstrung pearls down their cheeks, flushed red from the emotion. Abu al-Hasan commented on the marvel of their case, suggesting they enjoy each moment together since such moments are fleeting.
paragraphs.zh: 阿里宣誓他将永远爱着沙姆直至生命最后一刻，因为她的爱已经征服了他的灵魂。他们的眼泪如未穿线的珍珠般顺着脸颊滚落，脸颊因情感激动而泛红。阿布·哈桑对他们的故事赞叹不已，建议他们珍惜每一刻相聚的时光，因为这样的时刻转瞬即逝。

paragraphs.en: Morning interrupted Shahrazad's story, but Dinarzad praised it as strange and entertaining. Shahrazad promised to tell an even better tale the next night if she lived.
paragraphs.zh: 晨光打断了沙赫拉兹阿德的故事，但丁扎扎德称赞它新奇且引人入胜。沙赫拉兹阿德承诺如果她活到第二天晚上，还会讲一个更精彩的故事。

paragraphs.en: Shams al-Nahar signaled the first girl, who brought a silver tray with food. The guests ate while Shams and Nur al-Din Ali fed each other. Afterward, maids removed the tray and brought in three gold trays with different wines.
paragraphs.zh: 莎姆斯·纳哈尔示意第一个女孩端上一个银托盘，上面摆着食物。客人们用餐时，莎姆斯和努尔丁·阿里相互喂食。随后，侍女们撤走了银托盘，并带来了三个金托盘，每个多盛着一种不同的酒。

paragraphs.en: Shams ordered ten maids to serve and ten singers to join them.
paragraphs.zh: 沙姆斯命令十名婢女伺候，并让十名歌伎加入其中。

paragraphs.en: Shams asked one of the girls to sing. She sang: My life for him who greeted back with smiles, Turning despair into a happy hope. When he appeared, I could no longer hide My secret love from my critic nor cope.
paragraphs.zh: 沙姆斯让其中一个女孩唱歌。她唱道：“为了那个以微笑回应的人，我愿付出我的生命，将绝望转化为希望的曙光。当他出现时，我再也无法隐藏对他的秘密爱恋，也无法面对批评者。”

paragraphs.en: My tears of passion pressed between us twain, As if for him they too felt lovers’ pain.
paragraphs.zh: 我的热泪在我们之间流淌，仿佛也为他感受到了情人的痛苦。

paragraphs.en: Shams drank and kissed the cup before giving it to Nur al-Din Ali. She then asked another girl to sing: My flowing tears resembled the red wine, And my eyes brimmed e’en as the brimming cup. By God, I know not whether 'tis wine they shed, Or whether it is on my tears I sup.
paragraphs.zh: 莎姆斯喝了一口杯中的酒，然后亲吻了杯子，才递给努尔·丁·阿里。接着她让另一个女孩唱歌：“我的泪水如红酒般流淌，眼眶盈满了酒液般的泪珠。天地可鉴，我不知道是他们洒下了酒，还是我在啜饮自己的泪水。”

paragraphs.en: Nur al-Din Ali drank and Shams took a new cup. She kissed it and gave it to Abu al-Hasan ibn-Tahir. Then she sang: Oddly, his flowing tears course down his cheeks, And painful passion burns within his heart.
paragraphs.zh: 努尔丁·阿里喝着酒，沙姆斯换上新杯。她亲吻了一下杯子，然后递给阿布·阿哈桑·本泰赫。接着她唱道：奇怪的是，他的泪水如泉水般流下脸颊，而痛苦的激情在他心中燃烧。

paragraphs.en: Fearing to lose her; thus he always weeps Whether they are together or apart.
paragraphs.zh: 生怕失去她，因此无论在一起还是分开，他总是泪流满面。

paragraphs.en: Nur al-Din Ali ibn-Bakkar and his companion were captivated by a slave-girl's performance. Her voice harmonized with the music, and her skill left them entranced as if they had lost their ability to move.
paragraphs.zh: 努尔丁·阿里·本巴卡与他的同伴被一名奴婢的表演深深吸引。她的歌声与音乐完美融合，技艺高超得让他们如痴如醉，仿佛连动弹一下都成了奢求。

paragraphs.en: Suddenly, a girl appeared, rushing in like a bee and trembling like a palm tree. She announced that Afif, Masrur, Wasif, and other eunuchs of the Commander of the Faithful were at the door. The two men panicked, fearing discovery.
paragraphs.zh: 突然，一个女孩冲了进来，像蜜蜂般急促，又像棕榈树般颤抖。她宣布说，忠诚信徒的指挥官的太监阿菲夫、马斯鲁尔、瓦西夫以及其他太监都在门外等候。两人顿时慌了神，担心会被发现。

paragraphs.en: Their joy turned to dread as they nearly collapsed with anxiety.
paragraphs.zh: 他们的喜悦转为恐惧，几乎被焦虑折磨得支撑不住。

paragraphs.en: Shams al-Nahar laughed at their reaction.
paragraphs.zh: 莎姆斯·纳哈尔看着他们的反应，不禁笑出声来。

paragraphs.en: Morning came, and Shahrazad fell silent. Dinarzad remarked, "What a strange and delightful story!" Shahrazad replied, "Wait until tomorrow night; I have an even more fascinating tale if the king spares me."
paragraphs.zh: 晨光初现，沙赫拉兹默不作声。迪纳兹德remarked道：“这真是个奇特而迷人的故事！”沙赫拉兹答道：“等到明天晚上再说吧；如果国王饶恕我，我还有一番更加引人入胜的故事。”

paragraphs.en: I heard, O happy King, that Ali ibn-Bakkar and his friend Abu al-Hasan al-’Attar were terrified when they heard the girl's words. Shams al-Nahar laughed and instructed her to stall them while she covered their tracks.
paragraphs.zh: 我听说，幸福的国王啊，阿里·本·巴卡尔和他的朋友阿布·阿哈桑·阿特尔听到那个女孩的话后惊恐万分。沙姆斯·纳哈尔笑了，吩咐她拖延他们的时间，自己则设法掩藏他们的行踪。

paragraphs.en: Still looking at the young man, Shams al-Nahar forced herself to rise. She ordered the alcove doors shut and the drapes drawn, then closed the hall doors behind her before stepping into the garden. The couches were removed, and she seated herself, asking one of her maids to rub her feet.
paragraphs.zh: 莎姆斯·纳哈尔 still 注视着那年轻人，勉强让自己站起身来。她命令屏风门关上，窗帘拉紧，随后又把厅门关好，才走进花园。她让人搬走了榻凳，自己坐了下来，并让一个婢女为她按摩双脚。

paragraphs.en: Shams al-Nahar then summoned a maid to allow Ali ibn-Bakkar and his friend to enter. Three chief eunuchs, accompanied by twenty others in elegant uniforms with golden belts and swords, entered and saluted her. She returned the salute and received them warmly.
paragraphs.zh: 莎姆斯·纳哈尔随后召唤了一名婢女，允许阿里·本巴卡和他的朋友进入。三位主要太监在二十多位身着华丽制服、佩戴金色腰带和宝剑的同伴陪同下走进来，并向她行礼。她回礼并热情地接待了他们。

paragraphs.en: Turning to Masrur, Shams al-Nahar asked about his wish. He replied that the Commander of the Faithful wished to see her and spend the night with her. She kissed the ground before him, saying she would obey God's command.
paragraphs.zh: 莎姆斯·纳哈尔转向马苏尔，询问他的愿望。马苏尔回答说，信仰的捍卫者希望见到她，并与她共度一夜。她跪在地上亲吻地面，表示会遵从上帝的命令。

paragraphs.en: Then she instructed a maid to bring the housekeepers, who began preparing the garden and apartment.
paragraphs.zh: 随后，她吩咐一名女仆去叫来管家们，这些管家们随即开始打理花园和住所。

paragraphs.en: Shams al-Nahar told the eunuchs to return and inform the Commander of the Faithful that she was arranging the furniture and making the place ready, asking them to wait.
paragraphs.zh: 沙姆斯·纳哈尔吩咐太监们回去，告诉至高长官她正在布置家具，整理好一切，请他们稍候。

paragraphs.en: Shams al-Nahar embraced Nur al-Din Ali passionately and wept. He comforted her, promising patience until they could be together again. She feared for her own fate, knowing she would face the caliph's disappointment due to her love for Nur al-Din.
paragraphs.zh: 沙姆斯·纳哈尔热情地拥抱着努尔丁·阿里，泪水夺眶而出。他安慰她，承诺会耐心等待，直到他们重逢的那一天。她为自己担忧不已，知道自己因爱慕努尔丁而可能面临的哈里发的失望。

paragraphs.en: Abu al-Hasan al-’Attar advised Shams al-Nahar to remain patient that night and hoped their reunion was near.
paragraphs.zh: 阿卜杜勒-哈桑·阿塔尔建议沙姆斯·纳哈尔那天晚上保持耐心，希望他们的重逢为期不远。

paragraphs.en: A damsel warned them of approaching eunuchs. Shams instructed her to take the men upstairs, where they would wait until dark.
paragraphs.zh: 一个少女警告他们有太监接近。夏姆斯吩咐她带那些人上楼，让他们在那里等到天黑。

paragraphs.en: Morning came, and Shahrazad fell silent. Dinarzad praised her sister's storytelling, promising to hear more the next night if she survived.
paragraphs.zh: 晨光初现，沙赫拉兹德默然不语。丁纳兹德赞美姐姐的讲述技艺，承诺如果她能平安度过今晚，明天晚上还会再来听故事。

paragraphs.en: The following night, Dinarzad urged Shahrazad to continue the tale of Nur al-Din Ali and Shams al-Nahar.
paragraphs.zh: 当晚，迪纳兹德催促莎赫拉泽达继续讲述努尔·丁·阿里和夏姆斯·纳哈尔的故事。

paragraphs.en: I heard, O happy King, that the girl seated them in the gallery and left. They remained there until dark, unsure of what to do or how to escape. Suddenly, a hundred eunuchs entered the garden, dressed in colorful costumes and adorned with gold belts and swords.
paragraphs.zh: 我听说，幸福的国王啊，那个女孩把他们安置在走廊里后便离开了。他们在那里待到天黑，不知所措，也不知道如何脱身。突然间，一百名宦官进入了花园，身穿五彩斑斓的服饰，腰佩金 belt，并手持宝剑。

paragraphs.en: Following them were one hundred pages carrying camphor candles, and Harun al-Rashid himself, swaying between Masrur and Wasif, intoxicated. Behind him came twenty girls as beautiful as the sun, wearing fine clothes and sparkling jewels around their necks and heads.
paragraphs.zh: 跟随他们的是拿着熏香蜡烛的百人队，哈伦·拉希德本人则在马斯鲁尔和瓦西夫之间摇摆，仿佛陶醉其中。在他身后，则是二十位如同太阳般美丽的少女，身着华服，颈戴璀璨珠宝，头饰闪耀。

paragraphs.en: Shams al-Nahar met them under the trees, followed by girls with musical instruments. When she kissed the ground before the caliph, he greeted her warmly: "Welcome, my joy, my life’s bliss, and my heart’s delight." He leaned on her arm as they walked to a silver couch where he seated himself.
paragraphs.zh: 莎姆斯·纳哈尔在树下与他们相遇，身后跟着拿着乐器的女伴。当她在哈里发面前亲吻地面时，他热情地迎接她：“欢迎你，我的喜悦，我的生命之乐，我的心上人。”他挽着她的手臂，两人漫步至一张银色的卧榻前，哈里发坐了下去。

paragraphs.en: The other couches were placed beside the ponds, and the girls were seated in their proper places while Shams al-Nahar sat by his side.
paragraphs.zh: 其他座椅被安置在水池旁，女孩们各就各位，而沙姆斯·纳哈尔则坐在他的身旁。

paragraphs.en: After enjoying the garden for a while, Harun al-Rashid ordered the drapes of the alcove opened and candles placed on either side, turning darkness into light. The pages began to bring in the wine service. Abu al-Hasan later recounted: "I saw jewels I had never imagined before, dazzling my mind and heart with excitement.
paragraphs.zh: 在花园中流连了一会儿后，哈伦·拉希德下令拉开壁龛的帷幔，并在两侧放置了烛台，将黑暗变成了光明。侍从们开始端上酒水服务。阿布·阿斯兰后来回忆道：“我看到了许多前所未见的珍宝，它们让我心潮澎湃，目不暇接。”

paragraphs.en: Ali ibn-Bakkar, feeling weak and dejected, lay prostrate on the ground, unwilling to see what I saw or think what I thought." He said, "Do you see the caliph?" To which Ali replied, "He is the cause of our misfortune, and I am certain to perish.
paragraphs.zh: 阿里·本·巴卡尔感到虚弱而沮丧，瘫坐在地上，不愿看到我所见或思考我所想。“你看见哈里发了吗？”他问道。阿里回答说：“他就是我们不幸的根源，我确信自己将命不久矣。”

paragraphs.en: But only love and separation after union, the danger of the situation, and my own fear can undo me. May God deliver me from this predicament."
paragraphs.zh: 但只有爱与相聚后的离别、局势的危险以及我自身的恐惧才能将我击垮。愿上帝救赎我脱离这种困境。

paragraphs.en: Abu al-Hasan advised, "There is no recourse but to be patient until the Almighty God sends us relief." Then he turned back to observe the scene again.
paragraphs.zh: 阿布·哈桑建议：“唯一的办法就是耐心等待至高无上的真主赐予我们救济。”说完，他转身再次观察起眼前的情景。

paragraphs.en: When Caliph Harun al-Rashid requested a song from one of his damsels, she sang a poignant verse about unrequited love. Shams al-Nahar was so moved that she fainted and fell to the ground. Abu al-Hasan noticed her distress and saw his beloved unconscious nearby.
paragraphs.zh: 哈伦·拉什德哈里发向他的一位宫女请求一首歌曲，她唱了一首令人动容的情歌，讲述的是单相思的故事。夏姆斯·纳哈尔被这首歌词深深打动，竟然昏了过去，倒在了地上。阿布·哈桑注意到了她的不安，只见他心爱的人就在不远处昏迷不醒。

paragraphs.en: He thought fate had been kind but feared for their safety.
paragraphs.zh: 他认为命运对他们还算不错，但仍担心他们的安危。

paragraphs.en: A girl approached and warned them they must leave quickly, as danger loomed. She sprinkled rosewater on Nur al-Din Ali’s face and massaged his hands until he regained consciousness. The druggist urged him to wake up, warning that he could endanger everyone if he did not.
paragraphs.zh: 一个女孩走过来警告他们必须立刻离开，因为危险迫在眉睫。她往努尔·丁·阿里脸上洒了些玫瑰水，并按摩了他的双手，直到他恢复了意识。药剂师催促他快点醒来，警告说如果他不醒过来，可能会危及所有人。

paragraphs.en: Together, they left the gallery through a small iron gate by the river. A boatman arrived, and they boarded a rowboat. As they sailed away, Nur al-Din Ali recited verses expressing his longing for his beloved.
paragraphs.zh: 他们穿过河边的小铁门，一起离开了画廊。划船人赶到，他们上了一艘小艇。随着小艇渐渐驶离，努尔·阿丁·阿里脱口吟诵起表达对心上人思念之情的诗句。

paragraphs.en: Morning came, and Shahrazad paused her story. Dinarzad commented on how intriguing it was. Shahrazad hinted that tomorrow's tale would be even more amazing.
paragraphs.zh: 晨光初现，沙赫拉兹暂停了她的讲述。迪纳兹达对这个故事感到十分好奇。沙赫拉兹 aden 提示说，明天的故事将会更加令人惊叹。

paragraphs.en: The young man recited verses, and they crossed the river. Nur al-Din Ali remained prostrate before Abu al-Hasan, unable to stand. Abu al-Hasan feared robbers and reproached him until he finally rose and followed.
paragraphs.zh: 青年诗人吟诵着诗句，两人渡过了河。努尔·丁·阿里仍匍匐在阿布·哈桑面前，无法起身。阿布·哈桑担心有强盗出没，责备了他一番，直到青年终于站起，才跟随而去。

paragraphs.en: Abu al-Hasan visited a trusted friend on the other side of the city. His friend welcomed them warmly and invited them in. Abu al-Hasan explained that he had come with Ali ibn-Bakkar to avoid being discovered by a suspicious individual who intended to steal their money.
paragraphs.zh: 阿布·哈桑拜访了城对面一位可信赖的朋友。朋友热情地迎接了他们，并请他们进屋。阿布·哈桑解释说，他和阿里·本巴卡一起来是为了避免被一个心怀不轨的人发现，那人打算偷他们的钱。

paragraphs.en: Despite his efforts, they failed to find him.
paragraphs.zh: 尽管他们费尽心思，仍未找到他。

paragraphs.en: The host treated them generously and they stayed overnight. At dawn, they returned to the riverbank and crossed over. Abu al-Hasan led Ali ibn-Bakkar to his house, where the young man collapsed on a bed, overwhelmed by longing and exhaustion.
paragraphs.zh: 主人待他们十分慷慨，他们留宿了一夜。黎明时分，两人返回河边，顺利渡过。阿布·阿斯兰领着阿里·本巴卡来到自己的家中，年轻人一倒在床上，便被无尽的思念和疲惫压垮了。

paragraphs.en: Abu al-Hasan decided to entertain Ali with distractions, knowing well his feelings for Shams al-Nahar. He thanked God for their safety and pledged alms in gratitude.
paragraphs.zh: 阿布·哈桑决定用一些分散阿里注意力的事来款待他，深知他对夏姆斯·纳哈尔的情愫。他感谢上帝保佑他们平安无事，并许下施舍表示感激。

paragraphs.en: When Ali ibn-Bakkar awoke, I suggested he refresh himself. He requested water, performed his prayers, and then sought comfort from his friend Abu al-Hasan. Seeing this, Abu al-Hasan proposed that they spend the evening together for entertainment to ease Ali's suffering.
paragraphs.zh: 阿里·本·巴卡尔醒来后，我建议他先洗漱一下。他要了一杯水，做完祷告，然后向朋友阿布·哈桑寻求安慰。见此情景，阿布·哈桑提议晚上一起消遣一番，以减轻阿里的痛苦。

paragraphs.en: Ali agreed.
paragraphs.zh: 阿里同意了。

paragraphs.en: Abu al-Hasan summoned servants, invited friends, and brought a singer. They spent the night until candles were lit. The singer sang:
paragraphs.zh: 阿卜杜勒-哈桑召集了仆人，邀请了朋友，并请来了一位歌者。他们彻夜欢聚，直到蜡烛点燃。歌者唱起了歌：

paragraphs.en: "Fate pierced me with a deadly dart, And left me of my love bereft, Sick and impatient with my lot, The sorry lot I did expect."
paragraphs.zh: 命运用致命的箭射穿了我的心， 让我失去了所爱之人， 病态且对现状不满， 这正是我料想中的凄凉境遇。

paragraphs.en: Ali fainted upon hearing these words but regained consciousness at dawn. He asked to return home, and Abu al-Hasan allowed him to go.
paragraphs.zh: 阿里听到这些话后昏了过去，直到黎明才苏醒过来。他请求回家，阿布·哈桑答应了他的请求。

paragraphs.en: Shahrazad then paused her story, and Dinarzad remarked on its strangeness. Shahrazad replied that it was nothing compared to what she would tell the next night if she survived.
paragraphs.zh: 沙赫拉兹讲到这里停顿了一下，丁尔札德对这个故事感到十分诧异。沙赫拉兹 aden，如果她能活到明天晚上，她要讲述的故事将会更加离奇。

paragraphs.en: I heard, O happy King, that when Abu al-Hasan left, Ali ibn-Bakkar urged him to seek news of Shams al-Nahar. Abu al-Hasan believed her maid would inform them about her whereabouts.
paragraphs.zh: 我听说，幸福的国王啊，当阿布·阿哈桑离开时，阿里·本巴卡尔催促他打听夏姆斯·纳哈尔的消息。阿布·阿哈桑相信她的女仆会告知他们夏姆斯·纳哈尔的行踪。

paragraphs.en: After Abu al-Hasan returned home and waited for the maid in vain, he visited Ali ibn-Bakkar’s house early the next morning. Upon entering, he found Ali lying ill, surrounded by people and physicians.
paragraphs.zh: 阿bu尔-哈桑回到家后，等了那女仆一夜未果，第二天一早便前往阿里·本-巴卡的住所。进门时，他发现阿里病倒在床上，周围聚集了不少人和医生。

paragraphs.en: Abu al-Hasan greeted him with a glad look and asked about his health. After everyone left, Abu al-Hasan inquired if he had seen Shams’ maid. Ali replied that she hadn’t come yet.
paragraphs.zh: 阿布·哈桑面带喜色地迎接他，并询问他的身体状况。等大家都离开后，阿布·哈桑又问是否见到过沙姆斯的侍女。阿里回答说她还没来。

paragraphs.en: Ali wept bitterly, but Abu al-Hasan urged him to hide his secret and avoid scandal. Despite this, Ali continued to weep and recited verses about his love and suffering.
paragraphs.zh: 阿里痛哭流涕，但阿布·哈桑催促他隐瞒秘密，避免引起风言风语。尽管如此，阿里仍然泪如雨下，并吟诵起表达自己爱情与痛苦的诗句。

paragraphs.en: He said, "Life has dealt me a blow I did not need, and now death seems the easiest way out."
paragraphs.zh: 他说：“命运给了我一个本不需要的打击，现在死亡似乎成了最容易的选择。”

paragraphs.en: Abu al-Hasan comforted him, saying he was not alone in such trials. They conversed briefly before Abu al-Hasan went to open his shop in the market.
paragraphs.zh: 阿布·哈桑安慰他说，这样的困境并非他一人独有。两人简短交谈后，阿布·哈桑便前往市场开门营业。

paragraphs.en: Abu al-Hasan recounted that the maid greeted him looking pale and dejected. He told her about their journey, to which she responded with amazement. She then shared that Nur al-Din Ali ibn-Bakkar's mistress had fared worse after his departure.
paragraphs.zh: 阿布·哈桑讲述说，那女仆面色苍白、神情沮丧地迎接他。他向她讲述了他们的旅程，她听后惊讶不已。随后，她透露说，在努尔丁·阿里·本巴卡尔回家之后，他的主人娘子的情况更为糟糕。

paragraphs.en: Upon returning, she found her lady lying lifeless in an alcove, surrounded by weeping and rejoicing maids. The caliph, al-Rashid, was at a loss as to what ailed her.
paragraphs.zh: 回到家后，她发现女主人倒在壁龛中，周围是悲泣和欢庆的侍女。哈里发拉希德·阿尔-拉希德一脸茫然，不知发生了何事。

paragraphs.en: When the caliph asked Shams al-Nahar about her condition, she feigned recovery, kissed his feet, and claimed to have suffered from bile that made her faint. Al-Rashid inquired about her diet, but she avoided answering directly. Instead, she requested wine and insisted on resuming their festivities.
paragraphs.zh: 当哈里发询问沙姆斯·纳哈尔的身体状况时，她装作已经恢复，亲吻了他的脚，并声称自己因苦胆发作而晕倒。拉希德询问她的饮食情况，但她没有直接回答。相反，她请求赐酒，并坚持要重新开始他们的庆祝活动。

paragraphs.en: After the caliph returned to his seat, Shams al-Nahar sat beside him as instructed. Abu al-Hasan then told her of Nur al-Din's journey, causing her to weep when he recited Ali ibn-Bakkar’s verses. A girl named Lover’s Eyes sang a poignant song:
paragraphs.zh: 哈里发重新坐回座位后，沙姆斯·纳哈尔按照吩咐坐在了他的旁边。阿布·阿萨夫然后告诉她 Nur al-Din 的旅程，在朗读阿里·本-巴卡的诗句时，她不禁流下了眼泪。一个名叫恋眸的女孩唱起了一首哀婉的歌谣：

paragraphs.en: Life has forsooth not been sweet after you; I wonder how you have fared after me! If my loss you don’t mourn with bitter tears, Over your cruel loss my tears should blood be.
paragraphs.zh: 自你离去后，生活并未甜蜜；我真想知道你这些年过得如何！如果你对我毫不哀伤，不流下苦涩的泪水，那么我的眼泪应当化作血滴为你而流。

paragraphs.en: Shams al-Nahar swooned again upon hearing the song, and Abu al-Hasan tried to revive her. Shahrazad then paused, leaving Dinarzad intrigued.
paragraphs.zh: 莎姆斯·纳哈尔再次因歌声而晕倒，阿布·阿萨德试图唤醒她。沙赫拉兹这时停了下来，迪纳兹达不禁产生了浓厚的兴趣。

paragraphs.en: I heard, O happy King, that the maid said to Abu al-Hasan, "I tried to revive her by rubbing her feet and sprinkling her with rosewater. When she came to herself, I told her, 'Tonight you are going to bring ruin on yourself and all your household. By the life of your beloved, steel yourself and be patient, even though you are going through hell.'
paragraphs.zh: 幸福的国王啊，我听说女仆对阿布·阿哈桑说：“我试着用按摩她的双脚和洒上玫瑰水的方法让她苏醒过来。当她恢复意识后，我对她说：‘今晚你将自毁前程，连累整个家族。凭着你所爱之人的生命起誓，你要坚强些，忍耐些，即使你现在正经历地狱般的痛苦。’”

paragraphs.en: She replied, 'Can anything happen to me worse than death, which will deliver me from my torment?' While we conversed, another girl began to sing:
paragraphs.zh: 她回答说：“对我来说，还有什么比死亡更糟糕的事情，可以让我摆脱这种折磨呢？”我们在交谈的时候，另一个女孩开始唱歌：

paragraphs.en: 'Patience,' they said, 'may consolation bring.'
paragraphs.zh: “忍耐些，”他们说，“或许能带来安慰。”

paragraphs.en: 'Without him,' I replied, 'how can I patience find?
paragraphs.zh: 没有他，我如何才能忍耐下去？

paragraphs.en: For at our last embrace we pledged to cut
paragraphs.zh: 在我们最后一次相拥时， 我们就此许下誓言，

paragraphs.en: The cords of patience with the oaths that bind.'
paragraphs.zh: 忍耐的绳索与誓言相连。

paragraphs.en: Shams al-Nahar swooned again when she heard the song. The Commander of the Faithful rushed to her side and noticed how almost dead she seemed. He ordered the wine removed, each girl returned to her chamber, and spent the rest of the night with Shams al-Nahar, who remained unconscious.
paragraphs.zh: 当侍女夏姆斯·纳哈尔听到这首歌时，又一次晕了过去。真主至圣的指挥官急忙赶到她身边，发现她几乎失去了知觉。他下令撤走了酒水，让每个女孩回到各自的房间，然后整晚都守在夏姆斯·纳哈尔身旁，而她依旧昏迷不醒。

paragraphs.en: In the morning, when Shams al-Nahar awoke, the Commander of the Faithful summoned physicians to treat her, unaware of her passion. He stayed by her side until he thought she was beginning to feel better. Then he left a group of his concubines and maids with her before returning to his quarters, still concerned about her health.
paragraphs.zh: 拂晓时分，沙姆斯·纳哈尔苏醒过来，哈里发召来了医生为她诊治，全然不知她内心的渴望。他一直守在她的身边，直到觉得她的情况有所好转。随后，他留下了几位妃子和侍女照顾她，自己才返回寝宫，依然牵挂她的安危。

paragraphs.en: The maid then went to Abu al-Hasan and conveyed Ali ibn-Bakkar's message: "Convey my greetings to Shams al-Nahar; do all you can to counsel her; and spare no effort to keep her secret hidden. I myself will acquaint the young man with what you have told me about her."
paragraphs.zh: 女仆随后去找阿布·阿哈桑，并传达了阿里·本巴卡尔的口信：“请向沙姆斯·纳哈尔问好；尽你所能劝导她；务必竭力保守她的秘密。我自己会把你们谈到的情况告诉那位年轻人。”

paragraphs.en: Abu al-Hasan recounted his day of buying and selling before visiting Ali ibn-Bakkar. Upon entering, he found the young man in distress. Abu al-Hasan comforted him by saying that he would give his life to ransom him if necessary.
paragraphs.zh: 阿布·哈桑在拜访阿里·本巴卡之前，先讲述了他买卖奴隶的一天。一进门，他就发现那年轻人神情焦虑。阿布·哈桑安慰他说，如果必要的话，他会不惜倾尽生命来赎回他。

paragraphs.en: He then told Ali about Shams al-Nahar's maid who had visited him.
paragraphs.zh: 他随后告诉阿里，那名侍女沙姆斯·纳哈尔曾来访。

paragraphs.en: Ali's condition worsened; he fretted and wept, unsure how to handle this misfortune. He asked Abu al-Hasan to stay with him overnight, which Abu al-Hasan did, but slept little.
paragraphs.zh: 阿里的情况恶化了，他焦虑不安，泪流满面，不知如何应对这场不幸。他请阿卜·阿斯兰整晚陪伴自己，阿卜·阿斯兰答应了，但睡眠并不踏实。

paragraphs.en: At dawn, Abu al-Hasan left Ali and went to his shop where the maid was waiting. She greeted him and conveyed Shams al-Nahar's message that she was worse and had written a letter asking for an answer from Abu al-Hasan.
paragraphs.zh: 黎明时分，阿布·阿斯兰离开了阿里，前往自己的店铺，店里的女仆已在那儿等候。她向他问好，并转达了沙姆斯·纳哈尔的消息，说她的病情加重了，并写了一封信，请阿布·阿斯兰给予回复。

paragraphs.en: Later, Abu al-Rasan took the maid back to Ali’s house, but Shahrazad interrupted their story before it could continue.
paragraphs.zh: 后来，阿布·阿尔拉桑把女佣带回了阿里家，但沙赫拉兹德在他们的故事还没来得及继续之前就打断了他们。

paragraphs.en: I heard, O happy King, that Shams al-Nahar's maid visited Abu al-Hasan al-'Attar. He brought her to Ali ibn-Bakkar and left her outside while he entered the house. When Ali saw her, he recognized her and welcomed her with a wink.
paragraphs.zh: 我听说，幸福的国王啊，奴斯拉·纳哈尔的女仆曾拜访过阿布·阿哈桑·阿塔尔。他将她带到阿里·本巴卡家后，让她站在门外自己进了屋。当阿里见到她时，认出了她，并朝她眨了眨眼，表示欢迎。

paragraphs.en: "How is your master?" he asked. She handed him a letter from his friend, who explained his delay due to longing for Ali.
paragraphs.zh: “你主人怎么样了？”他问道。她递给他一封来自朋友的信，信中解释说因为思念阿里而耽搁了行程。

paragraphs.en: Ali read the letter, which began:
paragraphs.zh: 阿里读着信件，只见开头写道：

paragraphs.en: "In the name of the Almighty God,
paragraphs.zh: “至仁至慈的主啊，”

paragraphs.en: Answer the one who brings you news of me
paragraphs.zh: 告知你我消息的人，请你转告一声

paragraphs.en: And let his words suffice you for my sight."
paragraphs.zh: 让他的话代替我的所见吧。

paragraphs.en: The letter continued with expressions of deep desire and longing. It ended by saying that without this letter, the writer would have kept silent out of wisdom, but now he could not hold back his suffering.
paragraphs.zh: 信中表达了深深的渴望和思念。信末写道，如果没有这封信，作者出于智慧本会保持沉默，但现在他再也抑制不住内心的痛苦。

paragraphs.en: Ali then gave the letter to Abu al-Hasan, who read it with a trembling hand.
paragraphs.zh: 阿里随后把信交给阿布·阿哈桑，他颤抖着手读了起来。

paragraphs.en: Ali ibn-Bakkar received a heartfelt letter from Shams al-Nahar. Overcome with emotion, he replied tenderly and wept. He asked Abu al-Hasan to deliver his response.
paragraphs.zh: 阿里·本·巴卡尔收到了沙姆斯·纳哈尔的一封情意绵绵的信。他情绪激动地回信表达了深切的情感，不禁流下了眼泪。他请阿布·阿哈桑代为转达他的回复。

paragraphs.en: The next night, Shahrazad continued her tale. Ali ibn-Bakkar read aloud Shams al-Nahar's beautiful letter, then composed a reply filled with sorrow and longing. After finishing, he gave the letter to Abu al-Hasan, instructing him to pass it on.
paragraphs.zh: 第二天晚上，沙赫拉兹德继续讲述她的故事。阿里·本·巴卡尔朗读了纱姆斯·纳哈尔那封美丽的信件，随后自己写了一封充满哀伤与思念的回信。写完后，他把信交给阿布·阿 hassan，吩咐他转交过去。

paragraphs.en: Abu al-Hasan later recounted: "I took the letter and read its contents. It was a love letter from Shams al-Nahar, expressing her deep affection and his own intense feelings of longing."
paragraphs.zh: 阿布·哈桑后来回忆道：“我拿过信，读了里面的内容。那是沙姆斯·纳哈尔写的一封情书，表达了她深厚的爱情以及他本人强烈的思念之情。”

paragraphs.en: My heart aches for none since you left.
paragraphs.zh: 自从你离开后，我的心中再无牵挂。

paragraphs.en: O my lady, your letter has brought solace to my tormented soul. It has healed the wounds in my heart and brightened my eyes with its beauty. After long silence, I found myself moved to speak again.
paragraphs.zh: 我的夫人，您的来信抚慰了我备受折磨的心灵。它以美丽的文字治愈了我的伤痕，重燃了我心中的希望之光。久违的沉默后，我竟发现自己再次想要开口说话。

paragraphs.en: The more I read it, the more relief I felt. For I have suffered from a burning passion and an incurable longing since you went away.
paragraphs.zh: 我读得越仔细，心里的负担就越轻。自从你离开以后，我一直深受炽热的情感和无法治愈的思念之苦。

paragraphs.en: With saddened thoughts and exhausted body, My heart confused, mind demented by sorrow, I feel defeated in every grievance after your retreat. No complaint can quench this fire of desire, But it may ease the pain until reunion brings relief.
paragraphs.zh: 怀着忧伤的心情和疲惫的身体，我的心绪纷乱，思绪被悲伤扭曲。你离去后，我每桩怨诉都以失败告终。没有怨言能够熄灭这股渴望之火，但或许能暂时减轻痛苦，直到重逢带来慰藉。

paragraphs.en: The letter stirred me deeply. I gave it to Shams al-Nahar, who stepped closer as Ali ibn-Bakkar asked her to convey his greetings and share his sickness and love for his master. He wept, making both of us cry.
paragraphs.zh: 这封信触动了我内心深处。我把信交给夏姆斯·纳哈尔，她走近了些，阿里·本·巴卡尔请她转达自己的问候，并分享自己对主人的思念和病痛。他泪流满面，让我们俩都忍不住落泪。

paragraphs.en: After parting with him, I went out with the still-crying girl.
paragraphs.zh: 分手后，我带着仍在哭泣的女孩走了出去。

paragraphs.en: Morning came, and Shahrazad fell silent. Dinarzad remarked, "What a strange and captivating story!" Shahrazad replied, "Wait until tomorrow night if the king spares me."
paragraphs.zh: 晨光熹微，沙赫拉兹默不作声。丁纳兹德remarked道：“这故事真是离奇而引人入胜！”沙赫拉兹答道：“如果国王饶恕我，你明天晚上就能听到更多。”

paragraphs.en: I heard, O happy King, that when Abu al-Hasan left the slave-girl Shams al-Nahar, feeling depressed, he began to think about his situation and what the two lovers had done to him. He concluded that their actions would ruin his business and lead to his downfall.
paragraphs.zh: 我听说，幸福的国王啊，当阿布·阿哈桑离开奴婢夏姆斯·纳哈尔，心情沮丧时，他开始思考自己的处境以及那两情人对他的所作所为。他得出结论，他们的行为将会毁掉他的事业，并导致他的失败。

paragraphs.en: The next day, Abu al-Hasan visited Ali ibn-Bakkar. Finding the shop crowded, he waited until everyone left before approaching Ali. He complained about his predicament.
paragraphs.zh: 第二天，阿布·哈桑拜访了阿里·本巴卡尔。见店铺里人很多，他等到所有人都离开后才上前找阿里。他抱怨起自己的困境来。

paragraphs.en: Ali advised, "Listen! I have never seen or heard of one like you in your love. Such torment and weariness befit someone whose lover is insincere.
paragraphs.zh: 阿里建议：“听我说！我从未见过或听说过像你这样深陷爱河的人。这种痛苦和疲惫只有在爱人不真诚的情况下才应该承受。”

paragraphs.en: Your beloved loves you and wishes to be with you. If she were contrary, disdainful, and perfidious, what would happen to you? Rise, mix with people, keep yourself busy, go riding, exercise, or else you will surely destroy yourself."
paragraphs.zh: 你的爱人爱你，渴望与你相聚。如果她对你冷淡、背弃，那又该怎么办？振作起来，多与人交往，保持忙碌，出去骑马，锻炼身体，否则你一定会自毁前程。

paragraphs.en: Abu al-Hasan took Ali's advice and thanked him before returning to his shop. He followed Ali's counsel but the outcome of his actions was not known until much later.
paragraphs.zh: 阿布·哈桑采纳了阿里建议，向他道谢后返回了自己的店铺。他依照阿里的劝告行事，但结果直到很久以后才揭晓。

paragraphs.en: Abu al-Hasan had a jeweler friend who knew of his involvement with Ali ibn-Bakkar and Shams al-Nahar. One day, the jeweler inquired about her, prompting Abu al-Hasan to evade directly. He admitted knowing she was not well but could reveal nothing else except what only God knows.
paragraphs.zh: 阿布·哈桑有一个珠宝商朋友，他知道阿卜杜勒·哈桑与阿里·本巴卡尔以及夏姆斯·纳哈尔之间的关系。有一天，珠宝商询问起夏姆斯的情况，阿布·哈桑避而不答，只是含糊其辞地说她“well”并不好，除此之外一概不知，只能天知地知神知了。

paragraphs.en: Abu al-Hasan then shared his plan to settle debts, organize affairs, and move to Basra, living incognito until he saw how their fate unfolded. He feared the maid who kept their secret might betray them, leading to his ruin.
paragraphs.zh: 阿布·哈桑随后透露了他的计划：打算还清债务，整顿事务，并迁往巴士拉，在那里隐姓埋名，直到看看他们的命运如何演变。他担心那位掌握他们秘密的女仆可能会出卖他们，导致自己身败名裂。

paragraphs.en: His friend responded that this was a serious matter, advising caution and protection from harm. The jeweler promised to keep the conversation confidential.
paragraphs.zh: 他的朋友回应说这是一件严肃的事情，建议他谨慎行事并注意安全。珠宝商承诺会保密这段对话。

paragraphs.en: Morning came, and Shahrazad fell silent. Dinarzad remarked on the strange yet engaging story. Shahrazad replied that it paled in comparison to what she would tell later if she survived another night.
paragraphs.zh: 晨光初现，沙赫拉兹德默不作声。丁纳札德对这个既奇异又引人入胜的故事感到好奇。沙赫拉兹德回应说，如果她能再熬过一个夜晚的话，她要讲述的将会更加精彩。

paragraphs.en: The next night, Shahrazad continued:
paragraphs.zh: 第二天晚上，沙海拉扎德接着说：

paragraphs.en: I heard, O happy King, that after Abu al-Hasan confided his plan and asked for secrecy, he prepared immediately and set off for Basra.
paragraphs.zh: 我听说，幸福的国王啊，阿布·阿哈桑在透露了他的计划并要求保密之后，立刻做了准备，并启程前往巴士拉。

paragraphs.en: Four days later, a jeweler visited Ali ibn-Bakkar's shop but found it closed. He approached one of Ali's servants and asked to speak with his master. After receiving permission, the jeweler entered and found Ali lying on a pillow.
paragraphs.zh: 四天后，一位珠宝商来到阿里·本·巴卡尔的店铺，却发现门紧闭。他走近一名仆人，请求见主人一面。得到允许后，珠宝商走进店内，只见阿里正躺在枕头上。

paragraphs.en: Ali greeted him warmly, inquiring about his health and apologizing for any delay.
paragraphs.zh: 阿里热情地迎接他，关切地询问他的健康状况，并为任何延误表示歉意。

paragraphs.en: Ali expressed concern over Abu al-Hasan al-’Attar’s absence, who had recently left for Basra on business. The jeweler was unsatisfied with this explanation and sought detailed information from Ali, as they were close friends. Upon hearing the jeweler's concerns, Ali appeared shaken and admitted he knew nothing of al-’Attar's departure until then.
paragraphs.zh: 阿里对阿卜·阿哈桑·阿塔尔的缺席表示担忧，后者不久前因公前往巴士拉。珠宝商对这个解释并不满意，便向阿里详细询问情况，因为他们是亲密的朋友。听到珠宝商的关切后，阿里显得有些动摇，并承认直到此时他才知道阿塔尔的去向。

paragraphs.en: Ali recited a poem expressing his sorrow over losing loved ones: I wept for past mistakes when my loved ones stayed, But now that fate has taken them away, My tears fall for them always, shared by none.
paragraphs.zh: 阿里朗诵了一首诗，表达失去亲人的悲伤：当亲人还在时，我为过去的错误而哭泣；如今命运将他们带走，我的泪水永远独自流淌。

paragraphs.en: He lowered his head in thought, then turned to a servant and instructed, "Go to Abu al-Hasan ibn-Tahir's house. Find out if he is at home or on a journey. If he has left, discover where and why."
paragraphs.zh: 他沉思片刻，然后转向一名仆人吩咐道：“去找阿布·阿哈桑·本泰赫家。查探一下他是否在家，或者外出旅行。如果他已经出门，要查明他的去向和原因。”

paragraphs.en: The servant departed while Ali ibn-Bakkar sat conversing with Shahrazad. He seemed troubled, shifting his attention between her questions and his own musings.
paragraphs.zh: 阿里·本·巴卡尔坐在沙赫拉兹德身边闲聊，似乎心事重重，目光在她的提问和自己的思绪间游移不定。

paragraphs.en: Soon, the servant returned to report that Abu al-Hasan had gone to Basra two days prior. Outside, a girl was inquiring about him. She recognized the servant as one of Ali ibn-Bakkar's, though he did not recall her.
paragraphs.zh: 不久，仆人回来报告说，阿布·阿哈桑两周前已经去了巴士拉。外面有个女孩在打听他的消息。她认出了那个仆人是阿里·本巴卡尔家的，但阿里自己并不记得她是谁。

paragraphs.en: The girl claimed she brought a message from someone dear to Ali and stood at the door awaiting his response.
paragraphs.zh: 女孩声称她带来了某个与阿里亲近的人的消息，并站在门口等待他的回复。

paragraphs.en: Ali ibn-Bakkar instructed, "Bring her in." The servant returned with a girl who resembled Abu al-Hasan’s description but was even more beautiful. She greeted Ali ibn-Bakkar politely as morning approached.
paragraphs.zh: 阿里·本·巴卡尔吩咐道：“把她带进来。”仆人带回了一个女孩，她的容貌与阿布·阿哈桑的描述颇为相似，但更为美丽。天色渐亮时，她礼貌地向阿里·本·巴卡尔问好。

paragraphs.en: Shahrazad paused, then said to Dinarzad, "What an intriguing tale!" Dinarzad replied, "How can this compare to what you'll tell tomorrow if the king spares you? It will be even more captivating."
paragraphs.zh: 沙赫拉兹停顿了一下，然后对丁纳兹阿德说：“这真是个引人入胜的故事！”丁纳兹阿德回答道：“陛下饶恕你的话，你明天要讲的可要比这个精彩多了。那一定会更加扣人心弦。”

paragraphs.en: The maid entered and spoke privately with Ali ibn-Bakkar, who denied any knowledge of her claims. She then left, leaving him in distress. The jeweler later revealed that he had spoken to Ali about the maid's connection to Shams al-Nahar, the slave-girl of Caliph al-Rashid.
paragraphs.zh: 女仆进来后与阿里·本·巴卡尔私下交谈，但他否认自己知道她所言之事。随后女仆离开了，留下他心绪不宁。后来珠宝商透露，他曾与阿里讨论过这位女仆与 Rashid 哈里发的侍妾 Shams al-Nahar 的关系。

paragraphs.en: He showed Ali a letter suspected to be addressed to Shams by one of her maids. Ali became upset and worried but eventually asked for the truth. The jeweler promised not to reveal any secrets and recounted everything he knew.
paragraphs.zh: 他拿给阿里一封疑似写给夏姆斯的信，是从她的一位女仆那里得到的。阿里顿时心生不安，满腹疑虑，但最终还是要求对方说出真相。珠宝商保证不会泄露任何秘密，并详细讲述了他知道的一切。

paragraphs.en: Ali thanked him, invoking blessings on him and expressing trust in his generosity.
paragraphs.zh: 阿里向他致谢，祈求上苍保佑他，并表达了对他慷慨大方的信任。

paragraphs.en: Ali then recited a poem: If I claim to be patient since she went away, May tears and loud lament give me the lie. I wonder whether 'tis for a mere friend
paragraphs.zh: 阿里接着吟诵了一首诗：如果我声称自她离去后变得坚韧， 泪水和响亮的哀叹将揭穿我的谎言。 我不禁怀疑，这是否仅仅为了一个普通的朋友。

paragraphs.en: When Nur al-Din Ali ibn-Bakkar finished speaking, he fell silent for a moment. Then he asked, "Do you know what Shams al-Nahar said?" She replied, "No."
paragraphs.zh: 努尔丁·阿里·本巴卡尔说完话，沉默了片刻，然后问道：“你知道沙姆斯·纳哈尔说了什么吗？”她摇了摇头说：“不知道。”

paragraphs.en: He continued, "She accused me of conspiring with Abu al-Hasan and instigating him to go to Basra. She wouldn't listen to my protests and kept accusing me. Now I don’t know how to handle the situation in his absence since she liked him and trusted him."
paragraphs.zh: 他接着说：“她指控我和阿布·阿哈桑勾结，唆使他前往巴士拉。她根本不听我的辩解，一味地指责我。现在他不在，我不知道该如何应对，因为她很喜欢他，也很信任他。”

paragraphs.en: Shams al-Nahar's words left Nur al-Din feeling helpless. He said, "If you understand the situation, take care of it." She responded, "I will do my best to support you without exposing you or causing harm.
paragraphs.zh: 莎姆斯·纳哈尔的话让努尔丁感到束手无策。他说道：“如果你明白其中的处境，就尽力帮我吧。”她回答道：“我会尽我所能支持你，但不会让你暴露或受到伤害。”

paragraphs.en: With God’s help, I’ll resolve this issue for you." They embraced and kissed as they parted ways.
paragraphs.zh: 有神助，我一定帮你解决这个问题。”他们依依惜别，互致亲吻。

paragraphs.en: Morning came, and Shahrazad fell silent. Dinarzad remarked, "What a strange and entertaining story!" Shahrazad replied, "Wait until tomorrow night if the king spares me; it will be even more fascinating."
paragraphs.zh: 晨光初现，沙赫拉兹默不作声。丁纳扎德说道：“这真是个奇怪而引人入胜的故事！”沙赫拉兹回应道：“如果国王饶恕我，那就等明晚吧；故事会更加精彩。”

paragraphs.en: The following night, Shahrazad began: "O happy King, I heard that the jeweler said he left after receiving a letter. As he walked, he found this message on the road:
paragraphs.zh: 当晚，沙赫拉兹阿德开口说道：“幸福的国王啊，我听说那位珠宝商在收到一封信后离开了。他边走路边发现路旁留有这样一条信息：”

paragraphs.en: In the name of God, the Compassionate, the Merciful,
paragraphs.zh: 至仁至慈的真主名下，

paragraphs.en: My envoy brought me hope and joy, But I suspect he misunderstood something."
paragraphs.zh: 我的使者带来了希望和喜悦，但我怀疑他误解了什么。

paragraphs.en: My grief deepened as I read the letter, puzzled by its origin.
paragraphs.zh: 当我读这封信时，不禁更加忧心忡忡，对其来源感到困惑。

paragraphs.en: A maid approached, looking around anxiously. Seeing the letter in my hand, she came closer, saying, "O my lord, this is mine; please return it to me." I ignored her and continued walking, but she followed until we reached my house.
paragraphs.zh: 一个女仆紧张兮兮地走过来。见我手里拿着信，她走近说道：“我的老爷，请把这封信还给我。”我没理会她，继续往前走，但她紧随其后，直到我们到了我家门口。

paragraphs.en: She entered behind me as I sat down and said, "Listen! This letter has no value for you since you don't know its sender or recipient. Why do you keep it?"
paragraphs.zh: 她在我坐下后悄悄走进来，说道：“听好了！这封信对你毫无价值，因为你既不认识发信人也不认识收信人。你为什么要留着它？”

paragraphs.en: I replied calmly, "Be quiet and listen." When she sat, I asked, "Is this not Shams al-Nahar's handwriting, intended for Ali ibn-Bakkar?" Her face paled, and she exclaimed in alarm, "He has betrayed us; his feverish love must have driven him mad.
paragraphs.zh: 我平静地回答：“安静听我说。”她坐下来后，我问道：“这不是沙姆斯·纳哈尔写给阿里·本·巴卡儿的信吗？”她的脸色顿时苍白，惊呼道：“他背叛了我们；疯狂的爱情一定是让他疯了。”

paragraphs.en: He spoke of his feelings to others without caution, unaware of the consequences."
paragraphs.zh: 他毫不谨慎地向别人倾诉了自己的感受，全然不知会带来什么后果。

paragraphs.en: Shahrazad paused as morning approached. Dinarzad, intrigued, remarked, "What a strange and engaging tale!" Shahrazad replied confidently, "Wait until tomorrow night; I have an even more captivating story to share if the king spares me."
paragraphs.zh: 天色渐亮，沙赫拉兹停下了讲述。丁纳兹阿德饶有兴致地说道：“真是个奇异而引人入胜的故事！”沙赫拉兹 aden 信心十足地回应道：“等到明天晚上再说吧；如果国王能饶恕我，我还准备了一个更加扣人心弦的故事要与你们分享。”

paragraphs.en: The next evening, Shahrazad began: "Then she rose to leave but, considering her departure might harm Ali ibn-Bakkar, I said, 'Listen! The heart reveals that one must and can conceal secrets except for love. Love's telltale signs make it hard to hide.
paragraphs.zh: 第二天晚上，沙赫拉兹阿德说道：“然后她起身要走，但我考虑到她的离开可能会伤害阿里·本·巴克尔，便说：‘听我说！心灵揭示了这样一个事实：除了爱情之外，人们必须并且能够隐藏秘密。爱的蛛丝马迹使得隐瞒变得困难。”

paragraphs.en: You wrongly accused Abu al-Hasan; Ali ibn-Bakkar has never betrayed your trust. Give me a pledge to share nothing of your lady’s affairs with you, and I will justify his behavior.' She agreed, saying, 'None loses a secret in your care, and no one suffers disappointment under your watch.
paragraphs.zh: 你错怪了阿布·阿斯兰，阿里·本巴卡尔从未背叛过你的信任。给我一个承诺，保证不向你透露任何关于你夫人的事情，我就能为你证明他的行为。她同意了，说：“在你照料之下，没有人会泄露秘密；也没有人会在你的监督下失望。”

paragraphs.en: Proceed.'"
paragraphs.zh: “请继续。”

paragraphs.en: Shahrazad continued her story, hinting at what was to come.
paragraphs.zh: 沙赫拉兹继续讲述她的故事，隐隐约约地透露出接下来的内容。

paragraphs.en: The girl spoke to the jeweler: "If you tell me the truth, I'll also speak honestly and entrust our secret to your care." The jeweler recounted his dealings with Abu al-Hasan ibn-Tahir and how he met Ali ibn-Bakkar. He found a letter she had dropped, adding that this showed his good intentions in handling their affair.
paragraphs.zh: 女孩对珠宝商说：“如果你告诉我真相，我也将坦诚相告，并把我们的秘密托付给你。”珠宝商讲述了他与阿布·阿哈桑·本泰赫的交往以及遇见阿里·本巴卡的故事。他还提到自己发现了一封她遗落的信件，这表明他对处理他们的事情有着良好的意图。

paragraphs.en: The girl was surprised but insisted on swearing the jeweler to secrecy again. She sealed the letter and instructed him: "Tell him it came sealed; let him seal his reply too so I bear no responsibility." She left with instructions to visit before delivering it to Shams al-Nahar.
paragraphs.zh: 女孩虽然感到惊讶，但坚持要珠宝商再次对她保密。她封好信件，并吩咐道：“告诉他这信是密封的；让他也回一封密封的信，这样我就不负责任了。”随后她离开了，并嘱咐他先去见一个人再把信交给“白天之光”莎姆斯。

paragraphs.en: Shortly after, she returned with a sealed letter that read:
paragraphs.zh: 不久之后，她带回了一封密封的信件，上面写着：

paragraphs.en: "In the Name of God, the Compassionate, the Merciful:
paragraphs.zh: “至仁至慈的真主：

paragraphs.en: Our messenger, who kept our secrets,
paragraphs.zh: 我们的信使，保守着我们的秘密，

paragraphs.en: Has betrayed us in anger. Choose another we can trust.
paragraphs.zh: 竟在愤怒中背叛了我们。另选一个我们可以信任的吧。

paragraphs.en: I have neither broken a vow nor severed a friendship; I've faced only sorrow since parting. I long for my love but he is far away. You'll see from my looks and words my plight.
paragraphs.zh: 我没有违背誓言，也没有断绝友谊；自分别以来，我只尝尽了忧伤。我对他的思念溢于言表，但他却远在天边。从我的神情和话语中，你就能看出我的处境。

paragraphs.en: Peace be with you."
paragraphs.zh: 愿平安与你同在。

paragraphs.en: The girl then left, leaving the jeweler agitated.
paragraphs.zh: 女孩随后离开了，珠宝商心中满是烦躁。

paragraphs.en: The girl who shared the jeweler's sorrow wept with him. She instructed, "Do not meet Ali ibn-Bakkar or leave your house until I return tomorrow. He suspects me, and I have suspected him as well."
paragraphs.zh: 那个与珠宝商同悲的姑娘也流下了眼泪。她吩咐道：“你明天回来之前不要见阿里·本·巴克尔，也不要出门。他怀疑我，我也怀疑过他。”

paragraphs.en: The next day, she returned looking cheerful. Upon his inquiry about news, she revealed that she had spoken to her lady and assured her of their relationship with Abu al-Hasan's absence. She detailed the jeweler’s friendship, their shared secret, and how he found the letter.
paragraphs.zh: 第二天，她兴高采烈地回来了。当被问及消息时，她透露自己已经和她的女主人谈过了，并向她保证了自己与阿卜·阿哈桑不在期间的关系。她详细讲述了珠宝商的友谊、他们共同的秘密，以及那封信是如何被发现的。

paragraphs.en: Her lady was astonished but wished to hear it from him directly for comfort.
paragraphs.zh: 她的女主人惊讶不已，但仍希望直接听他说出来以求安心。

paragraphs.en: The jeweler hesitated, fearing such a high-ranking task. He said, "I am not like Abu al-Hasan; I tremble at the thought of entering the caliph’s palace." Despite his reluctance, she persisted, promising protection and safety.
paragraphs.zh: 珠宝商犹豫不决，担心承担如此重要的任务。他说：“我可不像阿布·阿哈桑那样胆大，一想到要进入哈里发的宫殿就心惊肉跳。”尽管他内心抗拒，她还是坚持要求，并承诺会给予保护和安全。

paragraphs.en: Each time he tried to go with her, he faltered. Finally, she reassured him, saying, "She will come to you; do not move from your place."
paragraphs.zh: 每次他试图跟她一起去，总是犹豫不决。最后，她安慰他说：“她会来找你；不要离开原地。”

paragraphs.en: She left hurriedly, then returned, warning, "Make sure no one is in the house; he might reveal us." The jeweler recounted: "I assured her there was no one. With great caution, she left and returned with a lady followed by two maids.
paragraphs.zh: 她匆匆离开了，随后又返回来警告说：“一定要确保屋里没人，否则他会把我们揭穿。”珠宝商回忆道：“我向她保证确实没有人。她小心翼翼地离开后，又带着一位女士和两名女仆回来了。”

paragraphs.en: Upon entering, the lady's perfume filled the room, and her beauty lit it up. I stood, offered her a cushion, and seated her. She remained silent until she was rested, then unveiled her face, which I thought resembled the full moon or rising sun.
paragraphs.zh: 一进门，那女士的香气便弥漫开来，她的美貌仿佛照亮了整个房间。我起身为她奉上坐垫，请她入座。她沉默了一会儿，直到似乎恢复了一些精神，才缓缓揭下面纱，露出的脸庞在我看来犹如满月或是初升的太阳。

paragraphs.en: Turning to the girl, she asked, 'Is this the man?' The girl confirmed, 'Yes.' I greeted her, and she responded politely, expressing confidence in my honor, loyalty, and generosity.
paragraphs.zh: 转向那女孩，她问道：“这就是你说的人吗？”女孩点了点头：“是的。”我向她问好，她礼貌地回应，并对我表达了信任、忠诚和慷慨的印象。

paragraphs.en: She enquired about my situation, family, and friends, and I shared my circumstances, adding that my other house was reserved for guests with nothing but what I had told her maid."
paragraphs.zh: 她询问了我的境况、家庭和朋友，我便将自己的情况说了出来，并补充说，我的另一处住所则是为客人准备的，里面只有她刚才吩咐给女仆的东西。

paragraphs.en: She then questioned my involvement in the affair, to which I replied. Afterward, she expressed sadness over Abu al-Hasan's loss and invoked blessings on him. She said, "Men share desires despite different situations; no task is accomplished without speech, no wish fulfilled without effort, and no rest enjoyed without toil."
paragraphs.zh: 她随后质问我是否参与了此事，我回答说。接着，她为阿布·哈桑的离去感到悲伤，并为他祈福。她说：“尽管境遇不同，男人们仍有共同的愿望；没有言语就没有事情的成功，没有努力就没有愿望的实现，没有劳作就没有休息的愉悦。”

paragraphs.en: Morning came, and Shahrazad fell silent. Dinarzad remarked, "Sister, what an engaging story!" Shahrazad replied, "Wait until tomorrow night if the king spares me!"
paragraphs.zh: 晨光初现，沙赫拉兹默不作声。丁纳兹阿德说道：“姐姐，这故事真精彩！”沙赫拉兹回答道：“如果国王饶恕我，今晚再听吧！”

paragraphs.en: The next night, Shahrazad began:
paragraphs.zh: 第二天晚上，舍赫拉查德开口说道：

paragraphs.en: I heard, O happy King, that Shams al-Nahar advised the jeweler. She said, "Trust her with everything she tells you or asks of you; she keeps my counsel and acts on my behalf." Then she left, barely able to stand.
paragraphs.zh: 我听说，幸福的国王啊，莎姆斯·纳哈尔建议那位珠宝商。她说道：“把所有事情都告诉她或让你知道；她会遵守我的嘱托，并代表我行事。”说完，她几乎站不稳地离开了。

paragraphs.en: Later, I visited Ali ibn-Bakkar's house. His servants rushed to greet me, leading me to him. He lay prostrate on the bed, visibly distressed.
paragraphs.zh: 后来，我去拜访阿里·本巴卡尔的住所。他的仆人们急忙迎了上来，把我引到了他面前。只见他平躺在床上，显然非常焦虑不安。

paragraphs.en: Upon seeing me, he said, "Welcome! You have kept me waiting too long and added to my worries." He continued, "Yesterday, the girl brought a sealed letter.
paragraphs.zh: 见到我，他说道：“欢迎！你让我等得太久，增加了我的忧虑。”他又说，“昨天那个女孩带来了一封密封的信。”

paragraphs.en: I am perplexed; Abu al-Hasan was of great comfort because she knew him."
paragraphs.zh: 我感到困惑；阿布·阿斯兰是个让人安心的人，因为她认识他。

paragraphs.en: I laughed, and Ali asked, "Why do you laugh at my tears and trials?" He then recited:
paragraphs.zh: 我笑了笑，阿里问道：“你为何嘲笑我的辛酸和苦难？”随后他吟诵道：

paragraphs.en: He who laughs at my tears would now have wept, Had he suffered like me the pain I know. For none can feel compassion for the damned, Save one like him who knows protracted woe.
paragraphs.zh: 倘若他曾经经历我如今的痛苦， 此刻定会为我的泪水而落泪。 无人能对受难者产生同情之情， 除非是像他这样的，深知长期煎熬之人。

paragraphs.en: When the jeweler returned home after speaking with Ali ibn-Bakkar, he found the slave-girl Shams al-Nahar waiting. She suggested they meet at her place for privacy, but the jeweler preferred his own house. The girl then went to inform their mistress of the plan and returned with instructions to prepare another house.
paragraphs.zh: 珠宝商与阿里·本·巴卡尔交谈后回到家，发现奴婢夏姆斯·纳哈尔已在等候。她提议在她自己的地方见面以确保隐私，但珠宝商更喜欢自己家。于是，女孩去告知她们的女主人这个计划，并回来带着指示准备另一处住所。

paragraphs.en: She also gave him money for supplies, which he refused.
paragraphs.zh: 她还给了他一些钱用于采购物资，但他坚决拒绝了。

paragraphs.en: Shahrazad paused in her storytelling as morning approached. Dinarzad remarked, "Sister, what a fascinating tale!" Shahrazad replied, "Wait until tomorrow night; I have more to share if the king spares me."
paragraphs.zh: 莎赫拉兹正讲述着故事，晨光渐渐临近。丁尔札德说道：“姐姐，这个故事真精彩！”莎赫拉兹 aden：“等明天晚上再听吧；如果国王饶恕我，我会带来更多有趣的故事。”

paragraphs.en: The next night, Shahrazad continued:
paragraphs.zh: 第二天晚上，沙海拉扎德接着说：

paragraphs.en: According to the jeweler, he returned home and was soon visited by Shams al-Nahar. She proposed they meet at her place for privacy, but the jeweler insisted on his own house. The girl then went to their mistress with a message and came back quickly with instructions to prepare another house.
paragraphs.zh: 据珠宝商说，他回到家后不久，莎姆斯·纳哈尔便来访。她提议在她那里见面以确保私密性，但珠宝商坚持要在自己家里会面。女孩随后去找了她们的女主人，并很快回来带着指示去准备另一处住所。

paragraphs.en: She also gave him money for supplies, which he refused.
paragraphs.zh: 她还给了他一些钱用于采购物资，但他坚决拒绝了。

paragraphs.en: I was still annoyed by her behavior when I went to my other house. I gathered all my utensils, borrowed fine gold and silver vessels, carpets, and other necessities from friends. When the slave-girl Shams al-Nahar saw what I had prepared, she was pleased.
paragraphs.zh: 我依然对她的行为感到不满，便去了我的另一处住所。我收拾好所有用具，借来了精美的金器和银器、地毯以及其他必需品。当奴婢夏姆斯·阿纳赫尔看到我准备的东西时，她显得很高兴。

paragraphs.en: I instructed her to secretly bring Ali ibn-Bakkar back with her.
paragraphs.zh: 我吩咐她悄悄把阿里·本巴卡带回来。

paragraphs.en: Shams al-Nahar arrived after evening prayer, accompanied only by two maids. The lovers stood still in passion before falling into a swoon. We revived them and they spoke softly for a while.
paragraphs.zh: 莎姆斯·纳哈尔在晚祷后抵达，只有一名婢女相随。这对恋人沉浸在情欲中，几乎昏了过去。我们唤醒了他们，两人轻声细语了一会儿。

paragraphs.en: Then I offered them wine; they drank and ate, thanking me. I took them to another room where they enjoyed themselves, forgetting their worries.
paragraphs.zh: 随后我给他们斟上了酒，他们喝了酒，吃了点东西，并向我表示感谢。接着我把他们带到了另一个房间，在那里他们尽情享受，忘却了所有的烦恼。

paragraphs.en: Shams al-Nahar then asked if I had a lute or musical instrument. I brought her one, which she tuned and played with great skill, singing verses that spoke of love and truth.
paragraphs.zh: 莎姆斯·纳哈尔随后问起我是否有鲁特琴或其他乐器。我拿给她一把，她调好音，演奏得十分娴熟，并唱起了表达爱与真实的诗句。

paragraphs.en: Morning came, and Shahrazad paused. Dinarzad remarked, "Sister, what a strange and entertaining story!" Shahrazad replied, "This is nothing compared to what I will tell you tomorrow night if the king spares me."
paragraphs.zh: 晨光初现，沙赫拉兹停了下来。迪纳尔扎德remarked道：“姐姐，这真是一个奇怪而引人入胜的故事！”沙赫拉兹答道：“比起我明天晚上要讲的，这简直不算什么。如果国王饶恕了我，你就能听到更多。”

paragraphs.en: She sang these verses:
paragraphs.zh: 她唱起了这些诗句：

paragraphs.en: I lay sleepless as if in love with lack of sleep, And pined as if pining was made for me. As my tears coursed over my burning cheeks, Who can at once in fire and water be?
paragraphs.zh: 我辗转反侧，仿佛沉溺于失眠之中， 渴望着无眠，正如为无眠而生。 热泪滚落，灼烧着脸颊， 谁能同时在火与水间找到归宿？

paragraphs.en: Her singing was so lovely that I had never heard anything like it before. Suddenly, we heard terrifying noises and screams, feeling as if the house might collapse. A servant rushed in to say some unknown men had broken the door and were raiding the house.
paragraphs.zh: 她的歌声如此美妙，我从未听过如此动人的声音。突然间，我们听到了可怕的响声和尖叫声，仿佛房子都要倒塌了。一个仆人冲进来报告说，有几个不明身份的男子砸开了门，正在抢劫房屋。

paragraphs.en: While a maid screamed from the rooftop, ten masked men with swords and daggers attacked us.
paragraphs.zh: 屋顶上一名女仆惊叫起来，十名蒙面男子手持刀剑突然袭击了我们。

paragraphs.en: Seeing them, I ran out of the house and sought refuge at a neighbor's home. Hearing an uproar inside, I concluded that the two lovers were found out and being seized by the chief of police. I hid until midnight.
paragraphs.zh: 看到这一幕，我赶紧跑出家门，躲到了邻居家。听到里面一片喧闹，我知道那对情人已被警方头目发现并捉住了。我藏身到半夜才敢出来。

paragraphs.en: The jeweler did not dare to leave his hiding place. When the master of the house came down and saw someone he didn't recognize in a corner of the hallway, he retreated with fright and returned with a drawn sword. He asked, "Who are you?"
paragraphs.zh: 珠宝商不敢离开藏身之处。当屋主下楼看到走廊拐角处有个不认识的人时，他吓得后退了几步，随即拔出剑来。他喊道：“你是谁？”

paragraphs.en: The jeweler replied, "I am your friend so and so." The man threw away the sword and said, "I am sorry for what has happened to you. May the Generous God restore your substance."
paragraphs.zh: 珠宝商回答说：“我是你的朋友某某某。”那人扔掉了剑，说道：“为你所遭遇的事情感到遗憾。愿慷慨的上帝恢复你的财富。”

paragraphs.en: The jeweler then asked who had raided his house. The man replied that they were the same men who robbed and killed others. They saw him bring in many fine utensils yesterday and plotted to rob him.
paragraphs.zh: 珠宝商随后问起是谁袭击了他的住所。那人回答说，袭击他们的人正是那些抢劫并杀害他人的同伙。他们见他昨天带进了许多精美的器具，便密谋要对他下手。

paragraphs.en: He thought they might have kidnapped or killed his guest.
paragraphs.zh: 他心想他们可能绑架或杀害了那位客人。

paragraphs.en: The two men visited the jeweler's house. Upon entering, they found it in ruins—broken doors and shattered windows. The sight devastated the jeweler, who worried about informing his lenders of their loss and feared for Shams al-Nahar and Ali ibn-Bakkar.
paragraphs.zh: 两人来到珠宝商的家中。一进门，只见一片狼藉——门板破碎，窗户也已碎裂。这景象让珠宝商心如刀绞，他担心向放贷人报失，又生怕牵连到奴婢沙姆斯·纳哈尔和阿里·本巴卡。

paragraphs.en: He also feared retribution from the caliph.
paragraphs.zh: 他还担心哈里发会对他的行为进行报复。

paragraphs.en: Turning to a neighbor, he asked for advice. The neighbor suggested patience and trust in God, noting that similar robbers had targeted others, including the police prefect's household and the caliph’s guards. The jeweler prayed for protection and returned home.
paragraphs.zh: 他转向邻居求教，邻居建议他耐心等待并信赖上帝。邻居提到，类似的强盗曾光顾过其他人家，包括警察长官的住所和王室卫队。珠宝商祈祷一番后，便回家去了。

paragraphs.en: Morning came, and Shahrazad fell silent. Dinarzad remarked on the story, to which Shahrazad replied that it was nothing compared to what she would tell later if the king spared her.
paragraphs.zh: 晨光初现，沙赫拉兹默不作声。丁纳兹德对这个故事发表了几句评论，沙赫拉兹达回应说，这和她日后若国王饶恕她的话要说的故事相比简直不算什么。

paragraphs.en: The jeweler, reflecting on his misfortune, felt overwhelmed by the day's events. People rushed to him from all directions—some offering comfort, others demanding their goods. He struggled to console and explain to them, barely touching any food throughout the day.
paragraphs.zh: 珠宝商回想起这一天的遭遇，感到心情沉重。人们从四面八方涌来——有人安慰他，有人则催促他交货。他勉强应付着这些要求，一整天几乎没有碰过食物。

paragraphs.en: The jeweler followed a stranger to an unfamiliar house, where the man insisted on moving on due to its lack of proper doors or seating. They wandered until nightfall, eventually reaching a riverbank. The stranger led him into a boat, which was rowed across by a boatman.
paragraphs.zh: 珠宝商跟着一个陌生人来到一座陌生的宅邸，那男子坚持认为这里没有合适的门和座椅，不适合停留。他们四处游荡直到夜幕降临，最终来到了河边。陌生人领着他上了船，由一名船夫划着船渡过了河。

paragraphs.en: On the other side, they entered a long street unknown to the jeweler.
paragraphs.zh: 另一边，他们走进了一条珠宝商不熟悉的漫长街道。

paragraphs.en: At a door, the man opened it and invited the jeweler inside, locking the door behind them with an iron key. Inside, ten men dressed alike greeted the jeweler, who sat down exhausted and frightened. They offered him water, which he drank, followed by food that they shared together.
paragraphs.zh: 在一间房门前，那人打开门请珠宝商进去，并用一把铁钥匙将门锁上。屋内，十名打扮相似的男子迎接了珠宝商，他疲惫而惊恐地坐了下来。他们递给他水，他喝了一口；随后又一起分享食物。

paragraphs.en: The jeweler reflected that his hosts had shown no ill intent by sharing a meal with him. After washing their hands, they returned to their seats. When the jeweler resumed his place, they asked, "Do you know us?"
paragraphs.zh: 珠宝商想了想，觉得主人请他共进晚餐并没有恶意。洗过手后，他们又回到了座位上。等珠宝商重新坐好，他们问道：“你认识我们吗？”

paragraphs.en: He replied, "I do not recognize you or the man who brought me here, nor do I know where we are." They said, "Tell us about your case without lying." The jeweler responded, "My situation is peculiar; have you any knowledge of it?"
paragraphs.zh: 他回答说：“我既不认识你，也不认识把你带到这儿来的人，更不知道我们现在身在何处。”对方说道：“别隐瞒实情，把你的事情告诉我们。”首饰商答道：“我的情况确实有些特殊，请问你们对此有所了解吗？”

paragraphs.en: They admitted, "We took your goods yesterday and carried off your friend and the girl in your house." The jeweler asked anxiously, "Where are my friend and the girl?" They pointed to two doors and said, "Each is in a separate room.
paragraphs.zh: 他们回答道：“我们昨天拿走了你的货物，还带走了你家里的朋友和那个女孩。”首饰商焦急地问道：“我的朋友和那女孩现在在哪里？”对方指了指两扇门，说：“他们分别被关在不同的房间里。”

paragraphs.en: We insist that no one else should know about them. Their fine attire has puzzled us; we have not harmed them."
paragraphs.zh: 我们坚持不让其他人知道他们的行踪。他们那精致的服饰让我们感到困惑；我们并没有对他们造成伤害。

paragraphs.en: Morning came, and Shahrazad fell silent. Dinarzad remarked, "What an intriguing story!" Shahrazad replied, "Wait until tomorrow night if the king spares me!"
paragraphs.zh: 晨光初现，沙赫拉兹默不作声。丁纳札德说道：“这故事真引人入胜！”沙赫拉兹回答道：“如果国王饶恕我，明天晚上再听吧！”

paragraphs.en: The next night, Shahrazad began: When the jeweler heard their words, he nearly fainted with fear. He praised them highly, but decided to tell the truth immediately rather than conceal it. He recounted his entire story.
paragraphs.zh: 第二天晚上，莎赫拉兹朵说道：当首饰商听到他们的言语时，几乎吓得晕了过去。他极力称赞他们，但决定立刻说实话而不是隐瞒。于是，他把自己整个的故事都讲了出来。

paragraphs.en: They asked, "Is this young man Ali ibn-Bakkar and this woman Shams al-Nahar?" The jeweler confirmed, "Yes, I have told you everything."
paragraphs.zh: 他们问道：“这位年轻人是阿里·本·巴卡尔，这位女子是夏姆斯·纳哈尔吗？”珠宝商确认道：“没错，我已经告诉你们一切了。”

paragraphs.en: They were upset and apologized to the lovers. Later, the jeweler said they had returned some of the stolen goods: "Part of what we took is gone, but here is most of your gold and silver utensils," they said, promising to take them to his other house.
paragraphs.zh: 他们感到不安，向这对恋人道歉。后来，珠宝商说他们已经归还了一些被盗的物品：“我们拿走的一部分东西已经不见了，但这里大部分你们的金银器皿都在，我们会带它们去他家。”

paragraphs.en: They split into two groups, one with me and another with Ali ibn-Bakkar and Shams al-Nahar. The latter were nearly paralyzed by fear but managed to leave the house. As we walked, I asked about the girl and their maids, but Shams al-Nahar said she knew nothing.
paragraphs.zh: 他们分成两组，一组和我在一起，另一组则与阿里·本·巴卡尔和夏姆斯·纳哈尔同行。后者几乎被恐惧冻僵了，但仍勉强离开了屋子。我们边走边谈，我问起那个女孩以及她们的女仆，但夏姆斯·纳哈尔说她什么也不知道。

paragraphs.en: We reached the riverbank where they made us board a boat with them. Once across, we found ourselves surrounded by horsemen. The robbers quickly took control of our boat while we stood still on shore.
paragraphs.zh: 我们上了他们准备的船，抵达河边。过河后，发现自己被一队骑兵包围了。那些强盗迅速控制了我们的船只，而我们在岸边愣住了。

paragraphs.en: The horsemen questioned us, and I reluctantly admitted to being kidnapped by these very men.
paragraphs.zh: 骑兵们盘问我们，我勉强承认自己正是被这些人大概劫持的人。

paragraphs.en: Shams al-Nahar approached the captain privately. He then dismounted and helped her onto his horse, followed by Ali ibn-Bakkar and me. We rode until reaching a spot where two boats were waiting.
paragraphs.zh: 莎姆斯·纳哈尔悄悄地走近船长，然后她自己下了马，由船长扶上了他的坐骑。阿里·本巴卡和我也随后上马。我们策马前行，直到到达一个停靠着两艘小船的地方。

paragraphs.en: We boarded one while the others went in another. The boatmen rowed us to the caliph’s palace, where Shams al-Nahar was taken off with the captain.
paragraphs.zh: 我们乘上了一只船，其他人则上了另一只。船夫划着桨将我们送到了哈里发的宫殿，随后莎姆斯·纳哈尔被带下了船，由船长领进了宫内。

paragraphs.en: We continued across the river to our quarter under guard. Exhausted from fear, we collapsed and slept through the night and next day. When I awoke at nightfall, Ali ibn-Bakkar lay motionless, surrounded by his household in tears.
paragraphs.zh: 我们被押解过河，回到了各自的街区。恐惧耗尽了我们的力气，我们瘫倒在地，整整一夜和第二天都昏睡过去。夜幕降临，我醒来时， Nur al-Din 脸色苍白，一动不动，家人围在他身边默默流泪。

paragraphs.en: They urged me to explain what had happened, blaming my presence for his misfortune.
paragraphs.zh: 他们催促我解释发生了什么，指责我的出现导致了他的不幸。

paragraphs.en: The next night, Shahrazad continued her tale. She recounted how the jeweler was questioned about Ali ibn-Bakkar but refused to disclose his story publicly. When Ali regained consciousness, he was sprinkled with rosewater scented with musk.
paragraphs.zh: 第二天晚上，沙赫拉兹德继续讲述她的故事。她提到珠宝商被问及阿里·本巴卡尔的情况，但拒绝公开透露他的经历。当阿里苏醒过来时，身上洒满了掺有麝香的玫瑰水。

paragraphs.en: The people then questioned him, but he was too weak and motioned for the jeweler to be allowed to leave.
paragraphs.zh: 人们随后质问他，但他已经无力反驳，只是示意珠宝商可以先行离开。

paragraphs.en: The jeweler emerged, barely believing his freedom, supported by two men. His family and friends were overjoyed upon his return, asking what had happened. He washed himself, drank wine, changed clothes, and blamed it on wine-induced illness.
paragraphs.zh: 珠宝商在两名男子的搀扶下走了出来，几乎不敢相信自己获得了自由。家人和朋友们欣喜若狂地迎接他归来，纷纷询问究竟发生了什么事。他先洗了个澡，喝了些酒，换上干净的衣服，然后归咎于酒精引起的不适。

paragraphs.en: For two days, he lay quietly at home, unable to do much.
paragraphs.zh: 他连续在家躺了两天，几乎什么也做不了。

paragraphs.en: As he began to recover, the jeweler worried about Ali ibn-Bakkar and Shams al-Nahar. He avoided their houses out of fear of meeting them again. He had repented his past actions, given alms for his safety, and accepted his loss with gratitude.
paragraphs.zh: 当他开始恢复后，珠宝商担心起阿里·本巴卡和夏姆斯·纳哈尔的安危。他为了避免再次遇到他们而避开他们的住所。他已经为过去的所作所为感到悔恨，施舍钱财以求平安，并心怀感激地接受了这场损失。

paragraphs.en: After enduring a difficult ordeal, Nur al-Din Ali ibn-Bakkar decided to visit friends in the cloth market for some respite. There, he encountered Shams al-Nahar’s maid and was startled by her presence. Frightened, he fled into a mosque, where she followed him.
paragraphs.zh: 历经一番艰难波折，努尔·丁·阿里·本巴卡尔决定前往布料市场拜访朋友，寻求片刻安宁。在那里，他遇到了沙姆斯·纳哈尔的女仆，并被她的突然出现吓了一跳。惊恐之下，他逃进了清真寺，而她紧随其后。

paragraphs.en: She expressed concern and asked about his well-being and that of Ali ibn-Bakkar.
paragraphs.zh: 她表达了关切，询问他的安危以及阿里·本·巴克尔的状况。

paragraphs.en: The maid recounted their escape: fearing capture by the caliph's officers, they fled over rooftops until finding refuge with sympathetic people who helped them reach safety early in the morning. At nightfall, she sent a boatman to search for Shams al-Nahar, whom they found safe and sound in a nearby boat.
paragraphs.zh: 女仆讲述了他们的逃脱经过：为了避免被哈里发的官员捉获，他们逃上了屋顶，在夜幕降临前找到了一些同情他们的好心人，帮助他们安全抵达。傍晚时分，她派了一名船夫去寻找沙姆斯·纳哈尔，最终在附近的一条船上找到了她，确认她平安无恙。

paragraphs.en: Shahrazad then paused her storytelling, and Dinarzad remarked on the strange tale. Shahrazad promised an even more amazing story if she was spared another night.
paragraphs.zh: 莎赫拉兹随后暂停了讲述，丁尔扎德对这个奇怪的故事发表了自己的看法。莎赫拉兹答应如果再给她一个晚上不被处死的机会，她将讲述一个更加令人惊叹的故事。

paragraphs.en: I heard, O happy King, that the girl told the jeweler she had helped Shams al-Nahar after seeing her. She gave him a purse of dinars, which he refused, then returned to lock the gate with two maidservants. They carried the almost exhausted Shams al-Nahar to bed and let her sleep for two days.
paragraphs.zh: 我听说，幸福的国王啊，那位女奴在见到纱姆斯·纳哈尔后帮助了她，并告诉珠宝商这件事。她给了珠宝商一袋第纳尔金币，但被他拒绝了。随后，她返回家中与两名婢女一起锁上了大门。她们将几乎精疲力尽的纱姆斯·纳哈尔扶上床，让她连续睡了两天。

paragraphs.en: When Shams al-Nahar finally woke up, the girl sprinkled rosewater on her face, washed her hands and feet, and changed her clothes. She then persuaded Shams to drink wine and eat food. The girl said, "You have suffered enough; death would have been easier."
paragraphs.zh: 当沙姆斯·纳哈尔终于醒来时，女孩在她脸上洒了些玫瑰水，帮她洗手洗脚，并换上了干净的衣服。随后，女孩劝沙姆斯喝点酒吃些食物，说道：“你已经受够了，死也许更好一些。”

paragraphs.en: Shams replied that she was sure she would be killed but managed to survive.
paragraphs.zh: 沙姆斯回答说，她确信自己会被处死，但最终还是奇迹般地活了下来。

paragraphs.en: The robbers took them from the jeweler's house, asking who they were. Shams claimed to be a singing girl, while her beloved said he was common. They brought them to their place, where fear kept them walking.
paragraphs.zh: 强盗把他们从珠宝商家里带走，问起他们的身份。沙姆斯自称是歌女，而她的爱人则说自己只是个普通人。他们被带到强盗的藏身之处，在恐惧的驱使下，两人默默无言地走着。

paragraphs.en: When the robbers saw Shams' jewelry and doubted her claim, she refused to speak. Her beloved remained silent too.
paragraphs.zh: 当强盗们看到夏姆斯的珠宝并怀疑她的说法时，她闭口不语。她的爱人也沉默不言。

paragraphs.en: The robbers then asked about the house's owner. They replied with a name, but one robber knew it and said he could bring back the man. The robbers separated them, promising their safety until they found out who they were.
paragraphs.zh: 强盗们随后询问房子的主人是谁。他们报了一个名字，但其中一个强盗知道这个名字，并说可以带那个人回来。强盗们将两人分开，承诺在查明他们的身份之前保证他们的安全。

paragraphs.en: Nur al-Din Ali ibn-Bakkar recounted his ordeal. His companion brought him to a group who, upon learning their identities, apologized and quickly arranged for a boat to ferry them across. A patrol captain then approached; Ali managed to convince the man that he had been drinking and visiting friends when the others arrived with him.
paragraphs.zh: 努尔丁·阿里·本巴卡尔讲述了他所经历的困境。他的同伴将他们带到了一群人的面前，得知他们的身份后，对方连忙道歉，并迅速安排了一条船将他们渡过河去。这时，一名巡逻队队长走了过来；阿里成功说服那人，说自己是在与朋友聚会时被其他人一起带来的，当时只是喝了点酒。

paragraphs.en: The captain agreed to help, mounting Ali on his horse along with another man, a jeweler.
paragraphs.zh: 船长同意帮忙，让阿里骑上了马，另有一名珠宝商同行。

paragraphs.en: Ali returned home without knowing what happened to the jeweler or himself. His heart ached for them, especially the jeweler who had lost valuable goods. He urged someone to take money and find the jeweler to inquire about him.
paragraphs.zh: 阿里回到家时，对珠宝商的遭遇和自己的情况一无所知。他心里牵挂着他们，尤其是那位失去了珍贵物品的珠宝商。他催促别人拿些钱去寻找珠宝商，并打听他的消息。

paragraphs.en: Shahrazad then paused her story, saying it was nothing compared to what she would tell the next night. Dinarzad praised her narrative but Shahrazad hinted at an even better tale to come.
paragraphs.zh: 莎赫拉兹随后停下了讲述，说这故事比起她第二天晚上要讲的可差远了。迪纳兹达称赞她的叙述精彩，但莎赫拉兹暗示接下来的故事更胜一筹。

paragraphs.en: The following night, Shahrazad began anew.
paragraphs.zh: 当晚，沙赫拉兹德又开始了她的讲述。

paragraphs.en: I heard from the jeweler that the girl returned with a heavy bag of money. She gave it to me and asked where we should meet. I suggested her coming to my other house, which I would secure immediately.
paragraphs.zh: 我从珠宝商那里听说那个女孩带着一大袋钱回来了。她把钱交给我，问我应该在哪里见面。我建议她到我的另一处住宅来，我会立刻确保那里的安全。

paragraphs.en: After counting the two thousand dinars, I felt relieved and distributed some to my family and creditors.
paragraphs.zh: 清点完两千第纳尔后，我松了口气，并将一部分分给了家人和债主。

paragraphs.en: Upon reaching the new house, I had workmen restore the doors and windows. Two maids were left to watch over it while others served me. Then, I went to Ali ibn-Bakkar's house.
paragraphs.zh: 到了新居之后，我吩咐工匠修复门窗。留下两个女仆看守房子，其余的则服侍我。随后，我前往阿里·本·巴卡尔的住所。

paragraphs.en: His servants welcomed me warmly. Entering, I found him bedridden but able to speak. Holding his hand, he thanked me for my visit.
paragraphs.zh: 他的仆人热情地迎接了我。进去后，我发现他躺在床上，但还能说话。他握着我的手，对我来访表示感谢。

paragraphs.en: Slowly, we helped him stand and walk a few steps. He then changed clothes and drank some wine, all to please me.
paragraphs.zh: 慢慢地，我们扶着他站立并走了几步。随后，他换上了新衣，并喝了一些酒，这一切都是为了取悦我。

paragraphs.en: We discussed the situation. Seeing him improving, I reassured him that everything would be fine. He asked about our past misfortunes but later apologized, asking for updates on his slave-girl Shams al-Nahar.
paragraphs.zh: 我们讨论了情况。见他有所好转，我安慰他说一切都会好起来的。他问起了过去的一些不幸遭遇，但后来又道歉，表示想了解他的女奴夏姆斯·阿纳赫尔的情况。

paragraphs.en: I recounted my journey and her experiences, which he praised as a testament to her generosity.
paragraphs.zh: 我讲述了这段旅程和她的经历，他称赞这充分体现了她的慷慨。

paragraphs.en: The next night, Shahrazad began her tale:
paragraphs.zh: 第二天晚上，沙赫拉兹德开始了她的讲述：

paragraphs.en: "O happy king," she said, "the jeweler told me that when Ali ibn-Bakkar heard about Shams al-Nahar's generous gift, he praised her greatly. He promised to replace all his lost items and then gave him gold and silver utensils, far exceeding what was lost. The jeweler felt honored and said he would risk anything for their happiness.
paragraphs.zh: “哦，幸福的国王，”她说道，“珠宝商告诉我，阿里·本·巴克尔听说沙姆斯·纳哈尔慷慨赠送的消息后，对她赞不绝口。他承诺会将所有丢失的物品全部补上，并且还赠予了金器和银器，远远超过了损失的价值。珠宝商感到十分荣幸，表示愿意为他们的幸福冒险。”

paragraphs.en: That day and night, the jeweler stayed with Ali, who lay weak and wept. As dawn approached, Ali spoke: 'Love must end in either death or joy. I am closer to death, which is better than this torment.
paragraphs.zh: 那天整夜，珠宝商都陪在阿里身边，只见他虚弱地躺卧着，泪流满面。黎明即将来临之际，阿里开口说道：“爱情终将归于死亡或喜悦。我更接近死亡，而死亡比这种煎熬要好得多。”

paragraphs.en: If you help us meet again, our fate will repeat. How can I endure this agony a third time? I have no excuse after God's warning.
paragraphs.zh: 如果你能帮我们再次相见，我们的命运将会重演。我怎能第三次忍受这种煎熬？连上帝的警告我都无法为之辩解。

paragraphs.en: I fear for my life and do not know how to escape this predicament.'
paragraphs.zh: 我生怕不测，不知该如何摆脱这困境。

paragraphs.en: Ali then recited:
paragraphs.zh: 阿里随后吟诵道：

paragraphs.en: How can the sad do anything but weep? I yearn to let you know my love, and mourn, And wake all night, as if the night has said, ‘O stars, stay fixed and do not heed the morn.’
paragraphs.zh: 悲伤之人又能做何事，不就是哭泣吗？我渴望向你倾诉我的爱恋与哀愁，彻夜难眠，仿佛夜空在低语：“哦，星辰，请你们固定在此，不要理会黎明的到来。”

paragraphs.en: Nur al-Din Ali ibn-Bakkar said to his wife, "Steel yourself; bear both joy and sorrow calmly." He then recited a poem about enduring tears and sorrow.
paragraphs.zh: 努尔丁·阿里·本巴卡对妻子说：“振作起来；要平静地承受欢乐与悲伤。”随后，他朗诵了一首关于忍受泪水和痛苦的诗。

paragraphs.en: Shahrazad suggested going to the house where the slave-girl Shams al-Nahar lived. She might bring news. Nur al-Din agreed but urged her to return quickly.
paragraphs.zh: 沙赫拉兹阿德建议去奴隶 girl 聂萨姆·纳哈尔住的那户人家。她或许能带来些消息。努尔丁同意了，但催促她尽快回来。

paragraphs.en: At the house, Shahrazad found Shams al-Nahar trembling and crying. The girl explained that she had been beaten by the caliph's order after a gatekeeper overheard her talking about their secret meetings. The caliph then removed Shams' mistress to his own quarters with twenty eunuchs guarding her.
paragraphs.zh: 在王宫里，沙赫拉兹德发现夏姆斯·纳哈尔瑟瑟发抖，泪流满面。女孩解释说，她因一名守门人无意中听到了她们的秘密会面而被哈里发下令鞭打。随后，哈里发将夏姆斯的女主人带到了自己的住处，并派了二十名太监看守着她。

paragraphs.en: Shams admitted she didn't know how to help or what to do next, as no one was more trusted than her with her mistress's affairs.
paragraphs.zh: 沙姆斯承认自己不知道该如何帮助或下一步该做什么，因为没有人比她更受主子信任处理这些事务。

paragraphs.en: Morning came, and Shahrazad fell silent. Dinarzad praised the story, saying it was strange yet entertaining. Shahrazad replied that this was nothing compared to what she would tell the next night if the king spared her life.
paragraphs.zh: 晨光初现，沙赫拉兹默不作声。迪纳兹德称赞这个故事既奇异又引人入胜。沙赫拉兹回应说，如果国王饶她一命，她第二天晚上讲述的故事将会更加精彩绝伦。

paragraphs.en: I heard from the jeweler that Shams al-Nahar had warned Ali ibn-Bakkar to be cautious. She instructed him to prepare for danger or escape, as a serious situation threatened his life and possessions. Ali was alarmed and asked for details.
paragraphs.zh: 我从首饰商那里听说，沙姆斯·纳哈尔警告阿里·本巴卡警惕危险。她吩咐他做好防范或逃生的准备，因为一场严重的危机正威胁着他的生命和财产。阿里听到这些话后大吃一惊，连忙追问详情。

paragraphs.en: The jeweler advised him to take valuable items and trusted servants, then they planned to flee to al-Anbar by day's end.
paragraphs.zh: 珠宝商建议他带上贵重物品和值得信赖的仆人，然后计划在当天天黑前逃往阿安巴尔。

paragraphs.en: They set out but were attacked by robbers near dawn. Their camels, belongings, and money were taken; all servants were killed, and they were left naked. Ali ibn-Bakkar asked if this was worse than death.
paragraphs.zh: 他们刚出发，黎明时分便遭到强盗袭击。骆驼、财物和钱财都被抢走；所有仆人被杀害，他们自己也被剥得一无所有。阿里·本·巴卡尔问道：这比死还糟糕吗？

paragraphs.en: The jeweler said it was God’s will. They walked until morning, finding refuge in a mosque as strangers.
paragraphs.zh: 珠宝商说这是上帝的旨意。他们一直走到了天亮，在一座清真寺里暂避风头，当起了陌生人。

paragraphs.en: Morning came, but no one approached them. Suddenly, a man arrived after prayers and addressed them. Shahrazad paused her story, and Dinarzad commented on its intrigue.
paragraphs.zh: 晨光熹微，却无人前来打扰。突然，在祷告之后，一个男子走了过来，向他们打招呼。沙赫拉兹暂停了故事，迪纳兹德对这个情节表示出了浓厚的兴趣。

paragraphs.en: The following night, Shahrazad began:
paragraphs.zh: 当晚，舍赫拉查德开口说道：
